play_sequence.wait: Wait for the object response and next instruction before another sweep.

play_sequence.beat: At the waterfall stage, check the spoken downward-pull instruction against the animated guide and dirty lane.
play_sequence.input: Drag one finger downward through a single lane and release.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for lane feedback and speech completion; do not infer completion time from probe runtime.

play_sequence.beat: At the seahorse stage, check that the instruction names the visible rescue action and the seahorse remains the focal target.
play_sequence.input: Tap the indicated target once, then follow the activity's allowed tap/hold action as shown.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for the rescue response and next cue before repeating.

play_sequence.beat: After returning to a room, observe whether an actionable prompt repeats appropriately and still matches the visible target.
play_sequence.input: Re-enter through the ordinary route, then tap only the target indicated by voice and pointer.
play_sequence.wait: Allow the complete cue to finish; record replay and interruption behavior on-device.

code_constants.value: Contextual cue captions set the HUD message timer to 5.0 seconds when presented (scripts/audio_director.gd:102-110).
code_constants.scope: Code-defined caption lifetime only; L14 did not render the caption or measure speech duration or cue-to-pointer timing.

timing.assumptions: The helper's 10.542-second wall time in runtime/L14/attempt_1/receipt.json is isolated probe execution time, not gameplay duration. No audible timing was measured.

tactile.target_size: L14 sends no touch input. The live bathroom prompt is attached to a transparent one-finger basket Button whose source position and size come from BASKET_POSITION/BASKET_BUTTON_SIZE (scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_cleanup.gd:724-734); no phone-projected target dimensions were measured in this review.
tactile.press_response: Not measured. The probe invokes AudioDirector methods directly and records no rendered-frame response, visible cue, or physical input latency.
tactile.drag_hold_release: No drag, hold, or release path is part of this voice probe. The child-facing bathroom basket action is a tap in source; no physical touch was tested.
tactile.ownership: Not tested. The probe uses a synthetic voice pool and does not route touch through live Controls or test competing fingers.
tactile.cancellation: Not tested through the live route. Speech teardown and focus/pause cancellation were outside this probe.

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: a short spoken verb paired with an animated hand/pointer aimed at the matching object could help a non-reader choose an action without coaching. L14 verifies legacy cue selection/serialization, not that a child notices and follows the paired cue.
play_appeal.variety: The assigned probe has no gameplay action variety. The callers inspected point from a basket instruction into a tap, then use distinct skimmer-sweep, waterfall-pull, and seahorse-tap-fast instructions; whether this progression feels varied is unobserved.
play_appeal.world_response: Source routes current room prompts through a separate contextual cue catalog and leaves caller-owned visual guidance in place. The probe does not show or sound that response, so perceived world feedback remains untested.
play_appeal.replay: Not tested. The probe neither leaves/re-enters a room nor tests contextual cue replay policies in a new visit.
play_appeal.play_appeal_test: On the approved phone, invite the intended child to follow the fresh Day One route with no reading or adult instruction. Observe whether the child connects each spoken verb to the pictured pointer/target, acts, and notices the changed object. Repeat the focused bathroom basket and pool stage cues after a room re-entry; record where speech is missed, obscured, repeated, or points at a different action. Ask the child to show which action they want to repeat, without assigning a numeric fun score.

route_status.proven_scope: The one retained exact-Godot 4.7.2 headless run passed probe_day_one_voice: all 34 listed Day One required events resolved to their exact roshan_<event>.ogg filler paths and were classified as required; a repeated speaker prefix normalized correctly; generic talk resolved separately; generic talk did not replace a required line; and a second required line queued behind the first. The probe directly constructs ReefMain and AudioDirector and calls their resolver/voice methods.
route_status.route_gaps: This is not a fresh-save or child-visible Day One route. It does not enter the castle, trigger a gameplay caller, render a pointer, play audible samples through a device, or prove cue-to-pointer timing. Current bathroom and pool callers use say_day_one_context with day1_* cue IDs via separate catalog/routing code (scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_cleanup.gd:809-813,935-945; scripts/games/day_one_pool_cleanup.gd:559-575), which this probe does not exercise. Headless output is not Mobile visual, target-device latency/audio, child-comprehension, or owner-acceptance evidence.

sessions.focus: Day One revisit and repeat incentive

play_sequence.beat: Reach a room that has already been completed through the ordinary castle route; let any entry story clip finish.
play_sequence.input: Tap the visible completed-room destination once.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for the room-clean voice/message and the room's chosen fixture response to finish before tapping again.
play_sequence.evidence_limit: Proposed routed device observation; L15 did not execute this input.

play_sequence.beat: Check whether the completed fixture response is local and understandable as a room reaction.
play_sequence.input: Tap the same visible fixture once while it is idle.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for its authored sequence to settle; observe whether it starts the activity or changes completion/reward state.

play_sequence.beat: Visit the cleaned pool after Rumi has been met, using the visible room route.
play_sequence.input: Tap the pool destination once, then wait until the room entry transition ends.
play_sequence.wait: Observe whether Rumi is present before giving another input; no timing is inferred from the probe.

play_sequence.beat: Test the optional friend interaction without relying on its tooltip.
play_sequence.input: Tap Rumi once, release fully, then wait before deciding whether to tap again.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for the contextual greeting and visible burst to end; note whether the child understands that Rumi responded.

play_sequence.beat: Test a clean-room revisit loop for repeat appeal and safe exit.
play_sequence.input: Leave to the hall using its visible navigation, then re-enter one completed room and tap its fixture once.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for entry response and fixture settle; allow the child to choose another room or stop.

play_sequence.beat: Check a not-yet-unlocked destination's feedback against the actual next-step door.
play_sequence.input: Tap one visibly resting door once, wait, then tap that same door a second time within six seconds.
play_sequence.wait: Observe whether the local pulse and spoken guidance identify the active golden door; wait for the feedback to finish before following it.

code_constants.value: Completed-room entry requests the 'day_one_room_clean' message with a 6.0-second display duration (scripts/main.gd:6276-6278).
code_constants.scope: Code-specified message duration only; no speech length, animation length, cue alignment, or rendered timing was measured.

code_constants.value: Blocked-door feedback uses a 1.2-second SFX cooldown and a 6.0-second second-tap window (scripts/arena/castle_rooms_25d.gd:80-81).
code_constants.scope: These constants bound source logic, not a measured child wait or session duration.

timing.assumptions: No gameplay timing was observed. Receipt wall time is isolated probe execution time only.

tactile.target_size: The persistent Rumi hotspot is assigned a 240×240 base-coordinate Rect2 (scripts/arena/castle_rooms_25d.gd:86,2108-2112); projected size, overlap, and separation on Lenovo Tab M11 were not measured. Completed fixture target geometry was not measured.
tactile.press_response: Not measured with input. Source routes a completed-room entry to a message and fixture sequence (scripts/main.gd:6276-6278; castle_rooms_25d.gd:2031-2067).
tactile.drag_hold_release: No drag, hold, or release input is part of the assigned source-contract probe; the inspected revisit interactions are taps.
tactile.ownership: Not tested. No touch or competing-control event was dispatched.
tactile.cancellation: Not tested for hotspot press, fixture animation, room exit, pause, or focus loss in the live route.

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: a completed-room tap that gives a small room-specific fixture animation, plus a repeatable greeting from Rumi after the pool is clean, may let a child choose to revisit a familiar place and friend. This probe does not establish that the child discovers or values either response.
play_appeal.variety: Source maps bathroom, pool, stuffie room, and art room to different replay fixtures; the probe verifies the mapping appears in source but does not animate or compare the four responses.
play_appeal.world_response: Code maintains clean-room fixture feedback and conditionally adds persistent Rumi in the pool. Whether either response is visually legible or feels connected to the child's tap is unobserved.
play_appeal.replay: Repeatability is source-intended: completed-room feedback is invoked on room activation, and the Rumi hotspot increments a greeting counter on press. No actual repeated entry/press or cross-session replay policy was tested.
play_appeal.play_appeal_test: On the approved phone and an ordinary Day One save with at least one room complete, let the child choose whether to revisit a clean room and whether to tap its fixture or Rumi. Without prompting, observe whether the tap produces an understandable small response, whether the child explores another clean room, and whether the child chooses to repeat or leave. Repeat after leaving and re-entering, noting if responses feel fresh, redundant, or confusing. Do not assign a numeric fun score.

route_status.proven_scope: One isolated Godot 4.7.2 headless invocation passed the assigned probe's nine source-contract assertions. Those assertions search source text for bounded blocked-door feedback, a six-second completed-room response, fixture replay without launch/reward hooks, bathroom-navigation restoration, persistent contextual Rumi, protected-speaker exclusions, and a corrected art-studio prompt. The probe reads files and tests string conditions; it does not construct a gameplay scene or dispatch player input. The retained output is runtime/L15/attempt_1/probe.log.
route_status.route_gaps: The ordinary route is only traced from source: main.gd dispatches a completed room to the room-response method, while castle-room setup syncs persistent Rumi. No fresh-save visible navigation, completed-room tap, actual fixture animation, Rumi hotspot press, voice playback, render, or leave/re-enter/save-load sequence was executed. The runner reports headless=true and rendered_mobile_acceptance=false. Device touch latency/geometry, child understanding/replay choice, and owner acceptance remain untested; the probe's 0.573-second tool runtime is not gameplay duration.

sessions.focus: Grand Puff reaction window and mercy

play_sequence.beat: Reach Grand Puff through the normal Day One story route and let the automatic introduction finish.
play_sequence.input: Tap the visible active route/door when it is presented; then make no input during the splash.
play_sequence.wait: Wait until the splash closes and the movement cue is presented.
play_sequence.evidence_limit: Route suggested by main.gd:6742-6758 and dust_boss.gd:278-319; not traversed by this probe.

play_sequence.beat: Test whether the opening lesson accepts the child's chosen direction and makes movement the needed first action.
play_sequence.input: Touch one clear floor point away from Roshan and hold/drag briefly in that direction, then release.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for Roshan to move and for the first danger tell; no movement should mean the probe's documented lesson is not completed (dust_boss.gd:528-537).
play_sequence.evidence_limit: The internal probe automates stick movement; this proposed real touch check is not executed.

play_sequence.beat: Check the reaction window and boundary clarity on the first warning.
play_sequence.input: Move one finger to a visible floor point outside the glowing danger shape; keep it there until the bunny lands.
play_sequence.wait: Wait through the tell and strike; if the child stays inside, record whether the first warning pauses for discovery as source specifies (dust_boss.gd:398-410).
play_sequence.evidence_limit: Probe personas use analytic safe points (probe_dust_boss_balance.gd:82-90), so actual painted-boundary readability is untested.

play_sequence.beat: Check whether the counter is a distinct, intentional second action.
play_sequence.input: After a successful dodge, wait for the visible gold star, then tap once.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for the star's vulnerable animation and counter response; do not tap during the dim state (dust_boss.gd:498-526,690-714).
play_sequence.evidence_limit: The probe tests programmed counter delays and completion, not visual cue timing or touch-edge feel.

play_sequence.beat: Observe recovery after a bump or missed opening, then check whether mercy preserves a path to completion.
play_sequence.input: If the first attempt misses, follow the next visible tell and make one fresh movement/counter attempt; avoid rapid repeated taps.
play_sequence.wait: Wait through recovery and any broadened tell/counter window; note whether earned rounds remain and the next required action is clear (boss_encounter_2d.gd:58-108; dust_boss.gd:486-526).
play_sequence.evidence_limit: Scripted patient personas finish despite two simulated hits or misses; no human error-recovery or comprehension evidence exists.

code_constants.value: The warning profile defines 2.2–2.7 second attack tells, and the initial damage-recovery wait is 1.05 seconds (scripts/encounter_profile_2d.gd:21-24; scripts/games/dust_boss.gd:30,486-491).
code_constants.scope: Source timing only; a real rendered frame, voice, or phone was not measured.

code_constants.value: A successful first counter grants a 4.6-second landed hold while the optional dash cue is offered; later landed holds are 1.8 seconds (scripts/games/dust_boss.gd:551-569).
code_constants.scope: Code-defined hold; not observed by a child.

code_constants.value: Probe-reported simulated elapsed values range from 30.32 seconds (moving_masher) to 100.43 seconds (patient_both); the intended learning persona reports 34.93 seconds (runtime/L16/attempt_1/probe.log:4-11).
code_constants.scope: These are scripted encounter-loop measurements under Engine.time_scale=3 (probe_dust_boss_balance.gd:26-28), not real play-session or child attention durations. The probe does not assert the advisory 45–120 second band.

timing.assumptions: No gameplay duration is inferred from the helper's 242.138-second wall time. Probe persona seconds are simulated controller-loop elapsed values only.

tactile.target_size: No projected touch target was measured. Source grants a generous boss-card hit region with a minimum half-height of 64 screen units and a separate 56-unit top region (scripts/games/dust_boss.gd:676-688); those code thresholds do not prove physical target size or thumb reach on the Lenovo Tab M11.
tactile.press_response: Not measured from touch. The controller reacts to a tap in the live frame loop, but this headless probe sets action_down directly and records no rendered-frame latency (scripts/games/dust_boss.gd:235-275; probe_dust_boss_balance.gd:91-101).
tactile.drag_hold_release: Movement is represented by a continuous stick vector in the probe. The live source supports a world-move gesture and cancels it on release/teardown, but no finger drag, hold, release, or cancellation was exercised here (scripts/games/dust_boss.gd:640-655; probe_dust_boss_balance.gd:79-101).
tactile.ownership: Not tested with physical fingers or competing Controls. Persona inputs are assigned to shared touch_ui fields, so this run cannot establish one-finger ownership (probe_dust_boss_balance.gd:79-101).
tactile.cancellation: Not tested for real focus loss, pause, back, or scene teardown during a finger hold.

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: stepping out of a painted attack shape and choosing when to tap the gold star can feel like a readable two-part victory because movement and the counter each cause progress. The probe supports that cause-and-effect path in scripted controls; child agency is unobserved.
play_appeal.variety: Source uses circular warnings in the early phases and adds a lane warning in the final phase (scripts/encounter_profile_2d.gd:21-24). This could make the repeated dodge-and-counter loop feel newly demanding near the end; no player reported whether that change feels varied or stressful.
play_appeal.world_response: A successful counter changes the boss into a vulnerable laugh, plays Roshan's point verb, adds a sparkle response, and gives a landed breather (scripts/games/dust_boss.gd:498-507,657-675,551-569). The probe verifies completion, not that these signals are visually/audio synchronized or noticeable on device.
play_appeal.replay: Not tested. Each persona begins from cleared encounter save fields; no repeat visit, retained mastery, re-entry, or child-requested replay was observed (probe_dust_boss_balance.gd:45-55).
play_appeal.play_appeal_test: On the approved phone, observe an intended child entering via the ordinary Day One route with no reading or adult coaching. Record whether the child independently tries moving, recognizes the attack boundary, leaves it, then waits for and taps the gold opening; note whether the 4.6-second first landed beat supports noticing Roshan's result and the next prompt. Afterward, offer a return visit without suggesting it and record which moment the child chooses to repeat. Do not assign a numeric fun score.

route_status.proven_scope: The unchanged probe starts the live DustBossGame controller directly and runs eight scripted personas plus four negative controls on exact Godot 4.7.2. All 12 report OK and the terminal line is ALL OK. Attentive, learning, slow, slow-counter, patient-dodger, patient-counter, patient-both and moving-masher each reach three rounds; the two patient-both failures include two hits and two counter misses. Idle, stationary-masher, held-action and movement-only earn zero rounds during their bounded runs.
route_status.route_gaps: This is not proof of the visible Day One path: the probe skips the intro, obtains the DustBossGame from main, clears save state, and invokes _start_game_now directly (scripts/probe_dust_boss_balance.gd:26-55). Main's story caller starts it after the boss door is reached (scripts/main.gd:6742-6758). The probe assigns stick_vec/action_down rather than routing real touch through visible Controls. It provides no rendered Mobile capture, target-device input/audio or child observation. The matrix marks the encounter live, but this run does not establish fresh-save route discoverability.

play_sequence.input: At GLOVE GUIDE, press one visible glove, drag it toward its glowing mitt, then release.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for the glove return before pressing the other glove; no measured duration is claimed.
play_sequence.basis: The source contract permits completing the guide one glove at a time; the probe checks the released-finger path at scripts/probe_opera_gesture_quality.gd:1764-1778.

play_sequence.input: At JAB PRACTICE, press either glove, drag forward to the currently glowing pad, and release.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for the next pad to appear, then repeat until four intentional hits.
play_sequence.basis: Four-hit phase and target sequence are defined at scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:307-311 and scripts/opera_boxing_surface.gd:35-38,544-566.

play_sequence.input: On one jab, send repeated drag samples at the same target before releasing.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for release and return.
play_sequence.basis: Probe expects the accepted extension latch to bank only one jab despite duplicate samples at scripts/probe_opera_gesture_quality.gd:1727-1746.

play_sequence.input: At SOFT GUARD, move either glove into the currently highlighted guard bubble and keep it there through the counter check.
play_sequence.wait: The coded counter interval is 3.2 seconds; this is a source estimate, not a measured child wait.
play_sequence.basis: Counter checks glove distance, grants one guard when covered, then switches side at scripts/opera_boxing_surface.gd:343-363.

play_sequence.input: For one guard cue, leave both gloves at rest.
play_sequence.wait: Wait through one counter check.
play_sequence.basis: Uncovered contact routes to harmless feedback and awards no guard at scripts/opera_boxing_surface.gd:349-363; the probe's 12.8-second passive leg checks no passive progress at scripts/probe_opera_gesture_quality.gd:1715-1725.

play_sequence.input: Offer the next jab/guard opportunity and allow the child to decide whether to repeat, stop, or leave.
play_sequence.wait: Observe one complete response cycle only; do not coach or infer engagement from elapsed tool time.
play_sequence.basis: The two phases have distinct target verbs and explicit goals in scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:307-309.

code_constants.value: The guard counter interval is COUNTER_SECONDS = 3.2 seconds (scripts/opera_boxing_surface.gd:24,343-363).
code_constants.scope: Code interval only; not observed wall-clock cadence or child wait.

code_constants.value: Assist thresholds are FIRST_ASSIST_SECONDS = 5.0 and STRONG_ASSIST_SECONDS = 10.0; stuck time sets the demonstration/assist level at those thresholds (scripts/opera_boxing_surface.gd:22-23,320-329).
code_constants.scope: Source thresholds only; exact visible onset and interaction with a child's attempted movement were not rendered or timed.

code_constants.value: After a phase goal, the world requests 1.1 seconds before phase advance, or 2.2 seconds for the belt (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:3315-3319).
code_constants.scope: Code hold only; speech, animation, and overall career length were not measured.

timing.assumptions: No gameplay time was observed. Probe wall time measures the isolated scripted invocation only.

tactile.target_size: The radial acceptance radius is 78 base-canvas pixels initially, a 156-pixel diameter, and increases by 18 pixels per assist level (scripts/opera_boxing_surface.gd:599-600). Actual visible/hit alignment, projected size, overlap, and separation on device were not measured. Press chooses the nearest available glove without a distance cutoff (scripts/opera_boxing_surface.gd:441-457,501-516), so a bounded glove press region is not established by source.
tactile.press_response: A claimed glove follows its finger on drag and queues redraw; accepted forward reach emits a jab immediately in the same handler (scripts/opera_boxing_surface.gd:460-478,544-572). Probe assertions verified state changes, not rendered response frames or physical latency.
tactile.drag_hold_release: Jab requires a drag from the owned glove origin toward the active target; the extension latch prevents repeated drag samples from paying twice before release. Release clears that finger and the glove returns over subsequent process frames (scripts/opera_boxing_surface.gd:481-498,519-572). No biological touch feel or actual device drag was tested.
tactile.ownership: The source maps each finger ID to a distinct free glove and routes drag/release by that ID (scripts/opera_boxing_surface.gd:409-438,441-478,481-516). The probe directly checked two owners and releasing one while the other remains movable (scripts/probe_opera_gesture_quality.gd:1780-1804).
tactile.cancellation: Application/window focus loss calls cancel_all_touches, which clears both finger claims and resets gloves (scripts/opera_boxing_surface.gd:153-164,297-300). This invocation did not exercise actual focus loss, pause, close, or re-entry.

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: the child can choose which glove to move and make a visible jab, then decide whether to answer the slower guard cue; phase progress is emitted only after intentional movement. No child observed this.
play_appeal.variety: Source alternates among four jab mitt positions on accepted hits, and guard alternates sides after each successful counter (scripts/opera_boxing_surface.gd:35-38,204-212,353-363,560-566). Whether these changes look distinct or create a satisfying rhythm was not observed.
play_appeal.world_response: An accepted jab triggers a short impact response and advances the target; guard produces a pop and advances the side, while friendly contact preserves accepted progress (scripts/opera_boxing_surface.gd:167-176,353-363,560-572; probe log reports 274 checks).
play_appeal.replay: The source has phases with goals of four jabs and three guards, then additional modes; an intentional wrong move restarts the demonstration and raises assistance. Whether that loop feels inviting or repetitive is a hypothesis, not observed.
play_appeal.concrete_test_or_proposal: In a consented short play observation, let the child try one jab with either hand, notice the next mitt, and choose to continue or stop; then present one guard cue without coaching. Record whether the child independently repeats the visible glove-to-target action and notices the left/right change. If the three guard waits feel inert, test an earlier visual windup or nearby bubble pulse while preserving the existing harmless no-input outcome and requiring a real glove movement for progress.

route_status.proven_scope: One exact Godot 4.7.2-stable headless invocation ran probe_opera_gesture_quality.gd and reported ALL OK (274 checks). Source tracing confirms OperaCareerWorld2D defines the five Boxer modes and routes boxing gesture signals into phase progress. Focused assertions directly call the specialist's internal press/drag/release methods for jab, and the probe also covers both-glove ownership, passive waiting, render-path setup, and mouse fallback.
route_status.route_gaps: No fresh-save entry, visible career navigation, ordinary GUI touch route, rendered Mobile frame, actual voice playback, or full child-paced Boxer sequence was executed. The probe's internal method calls and 5.847-second runner wall time are not a play session or gameplay duration. Physical Lenovo Tab M11 target geometry/latency, a second aspect, child understanding/comfort/replay choice, and owner acceptance remain untested.

play_sequence.input: Enter the visible teacher career and let its first PATTERN board appear; allow the idle demonstration to run without touching.
play_sequence.wait: The probe simulates 30 quiet seconds with no win. Treat this as a negative assertion, not a recommended child wait; observe the first rendered cue and offer help if the child is stuck.
play_sequence.basis: Four one-goal lesson phases and armed opening are asserted at scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:2358-2374; idle no-award assertion at :2385-2392.

play_sequence.input: Tap one answer. If it is wrong, let the child tap another answer when ready.
play_sequence.wait: Wrong-answer feedback has a 0.4-second source timer; no measured pause is claimed.
play_sequence.basis: Wrong answer marks assistance and does not complete; correct retry completes at scripts/opera_teacher_surface.gd:173-205 and scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:2393-2404.

play_sequence.input: On COUNT, tap each visible counter once, then tap the answer that matches the counted set.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for one numeral/count response after each release; no measured rendered response time is available.
play_sequence.basis: Counter and answer requirements are checked at scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:2406-2435; count acceptance radius is 36 px in scripts/opera_teacher_surface.gd:165-169.

play_sequence.input: On ADD, tap the join action, then tap each object in the joined groups and choose the total.
play_sequence.wait: Wait at least the coded 0.4-second join gate before the first count tap; this is the source/probe threshold, not a measured child wait.
play_sequence.basis: Join-before-count behavior and 0.41-second probe advancement at scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:2437-2454; source gate at scripts/opera_teacher_surface.gd:157-164.

play_sequence.input: On MATCH, tap the shape matching the prompt; allow a second tap only if the first was not accepted.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for the completion response before another action; the probe confirms duplicate taps award only one completion.
play_sequence.basis: Four non-overlapping choice rectangles and one award are asserted at scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:2456-2475.

play_sequence.input: After one completed lesson, let the child choose whether to try another lesson or leave.
play_sequence.wait: Observe one choice without coaching; do not infer replay appeal from runner time.
play_sequence.basis: Probe confirms the four phase kinds but does not observe an ordinary visible career exit/replay route (scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:2358-2369; receipt states headless and rendered_mobile_acceptance=false).

code_constants.value: A touch release more than 38 base-canvas pixels from its press is ignored (scripts/opera_teacher_surface.gd:147-153).
code_constants.scope: Source threshold; not a measured hand/touch tolerance on device.

code_constants.value: Wrong-choice visual feedback is assigned feedback_t = 0.4 seconds (scripts/opera_teacher_surface.gd:179-186).
code_constants.scope: Code timer; rendered feedback duration was not observed.

code_constants.value: The addition groups join with a join_t = 0.4 second input gate (scripts/opera_teacher_surface.gd:157-164); the assigned probe advances this timer by 0.41 seconds before counting (scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:2437-2450).
code_constants.scope: Deterministic probe/code wait; child pacing was not observed.

code_constants.value: The idle negative assertion advances 60 × 0.5 seconds (30 simulated seconds) without a correct answer or award (scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:2389-2392).
code_constants.scope: Probe-simulated time only; not an observed play session.

timing.assumptions: No child-paced gameplay duration was observed. Receipt wall_elapsed_seconds records the probe process only.

tactile.target_size: Choice rectangles are 210×170 canvas px for two/three choices and 174×170 for four (scripts/opera_teacher_surface.gd:64-71); the probe checks four-choice containment and minimum size (scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:2460-2469). Counter touch acceptance is a 36 px radius, or 72 px diameter (scripts/opera_teacher_surface.gd:165-169), below StorybookUI.MIN_TOUCH 110×110 (scripts/storybook_ui.gd:23). This is a source-level target-size concern; rendered scale, drawn affordance, overlap, and device feel were not tested.
tactile.press_response: A valid release changes the count or choice state, emits progress, updates numerals and queues redraw (scripts/opera_teacher_surface.gd:165-194). The probe observed state assertions, not visible response within two rendered frames.
tactile.drag_hold_release: The lesson is tap-based: a press/release within 38 px is required; moving farther cancels that action (scripts/opera_teacher_surface.gd:140-153). Counting uses a single release within 36 px of an uncounted object; there is no drag-to-count behavior (scripts/opera_teacher_surface.gd:165-170). No physical touch was tested.
tactile.ownership: Screen-touch press claims the first available touch ID while touch_owner is -1; only that ID's release is handled (scripts/opera_teacher_surface.gd:207-218). Probe injects two IDs, confirms ID 9 cannot count while ID 7 owns the press, then confirms cancellation clears ownership (scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:2411-2420).
tactile.cancellation: Canceled screen touch and application pause/focus loss clear ownership and held state; checkpoint cancellation emits a progress snapshot (scripts/opera_teacher_surface.gd:123-127,207-218,230-233). Probe covers canceled input, not actual focus loss or pause/re-entry.

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: the child chooses answers and physically counts visible objects, then sees a result; addition adds an explicit join action before counting. Probe assertions establish state causality only, not that the child understands these actions.
play_appeal.variety: Pattern, count, add, and shape matching provide distinct prompt types under one repeated answer board (scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:2358-2369). Whether the shared format feels varied or repetitive is unknown without viewing and child play.
play_appeal.world_response: A wrong answer marks assisted and requests teacher_help without mastery; correct selection completes the lesson (scripts/opera_teacher_surface.gd:173-205; probe lines 2393-2404). Actual voice playback and animation were not verified.
play_appeal.replay: Progress records kind, sequence and tier, and partial count state round-trips through JSON in the focused check (scripts/opera_teacher_surface.gd:85-114; scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:2420-2435). The child-facing reason to return for later tiers is not established by this probe.
play_appeal.concrete_test_or_proposal: In a consented, short observation on the target tablet, show the ordinary teacher route and let the child choose among a simple pattern and counting lesson without explaining text. Record whether they discover tapping one object at a time, recover after one wrong choice, and independently ask to try another lesson. Specifically observe whether the small counter hit areas cause missed taps; if so, test a clearly bounded larger visible target layout while preserving separated counters and one-finger use.

route_status.proven_scope: The exact Godot 4.7.2-stable scripted probe ran once with an isolated profile and reported OPERA2D result ALL OK. Focused Teacher checks directly instantiate OperaTeacherSurface and call helper touch events; source tracing confirms the teacher surface is part of the current Opera career world and its four phases.
route_status.route_gaps: No fresh-save visible route into the teacher career or ordinary rendered touch route was executed in this session. Headless rendering does not establish Mobile composition, target alignment, response frames or actual voice playback. Lenovo Tab M11 latency/frame pacing, child comprehension/appeal, and owner acceptance remain unobserved. Probe wall time is not gameplay time.

code_constants.value: LAP_DISTANCE is 800 units and LAP_SECONDS is 24 seconds, yielding 33.3 distance units/second at the unboosted nominal speed; two laps therefore imply about 48 seconds of full-speed driving before countdown, acceleration, steering, turbo and pauses (scripts/opera_racer_surface.gd:10-11,278).
code_constants.scope: An arithmetic source estimate only; actual race and child session duration were not measured.

code_constants.value: The first accepted race touch starts a 1.5-second countdown, and released steering input has a 2.0-second grace window before the surface stops advancing (scripts/opera_racer_surface.gd:13,209-216,244-256).
code_constants.scope: Code constants/branches only; rendered cue timing and perceived pause behavior were not measured.

code_constants.value: RACE's career goal is two lap units (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:331-334); phase progress is derived from kart distance divided by 800, capped at that goal (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:3511-3515).
code_constants.scope: Source progress mapping; not observed gameplay duration.

timing.assumptions: No child-paced session time was observed. The helper's 23.843-second wall time is probe execution time, not game duration. The 48-second estimate assumes sustained nominal unboosted speed and omits the preceding two career phases.

tactile.target_size: The visible steering control is a 770×126 base-canvas-pixel horizontal strip, with a 794×150 accepted region after the code's 12-pixel hit expansion (scripts/opera_racer_surface.gd:14,146-148,439-452). Turbo is a 120-pixel diameter circle (center 1134,632; radius 60; lines 15-16,455-464). These are logical canvas dimensions; projection, spacing and one-finger comfort on the Lenovo Tab M11 were not tested.
tactile.press_response: A press inside the steering strip starts the race and 1.5-second countdown; drag immediately updates the steering value and queues redraw (scripts/opera_racer_surface.gd:172-196,209-216). The probe verifies state transitions, not visible response frames or physical latency.
tactile.drag_hold_release: Horizontal position maps to steering from -1 to +1; releasing clears held state and centers steering. While held, driving input remains active; after release, the 2-second grace expires and the race pauses (scripts/opera_racer_surface.gd:189-210,244-249). The probe uses small repeated horizontal drags while retaining ownership; real finger comfort was not tested.
tactile.ownership: The steering touch index and Turbo touch index are tracked independently. The probe's synthetic second touch fires Turbo while preserving the steering owner's drag, and an unrelated drag ID is ignored (scripts/opera_racer_surface.gd:136-156; scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:2071-2085; L19 probe.log:1030).
tactile.cancellation: cancel_race_touch clears steering, Turbo and input grace; application pause/focus-out invokes it (scripts/opera_racer_surface.gd:219-233). Probe coverage confirms a direct cancel freezes distance and a fresh touch resumes, then cancellation/re-entry cleanup (scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:1980-2028; L19 probe.log:1404-1412). Actual app pause/focus transitions on device were not exercised in this focused input leg.

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: a long steering bar, visible moving wheel/knob and coral-gate instruction may let a child feel that small left/right swipes guide Roshan's kart. The probe establishes that synthetic owned steering inputs can move the kart to the two-lap finish, not that a child understands or enjoys it.
play_appeal.variety: Hypothesis: alternating bends, lap markers, pearls, boost strips and the rival could make repeated steering feel varied; no rendered sequence or child choice was observed.
play_appeal.world_response: Source emits lap, pearl and Turbo events and paints lap progress/collection/boost effects (scripts/opera_racer_surface.gd:267-337,419-464). The probe checks causal inside-line pace and pearl payoff (L19 probe.log:1413), but not their legibility or sound in play.
play_appeal.replay: The probe confirms clean scripted cancel/re-entry and trophy recovery (L19 probe.log:1404-1412). Whether the child chooses another race, or whether the race feels too long or repetitive, remains unknown.
play_appeal.concrete_test_or_proposal: On the exact Lenovo Tab M11 build, observe a consented non-reader entering through the normal Movie Lounge route and receiving no adult coaching. Check whether the child independently uses the pictured steering bar, notices the lap markers, can resume after a brief lift, and chooses whether to replay. Separately run a controlled race where the imp reaches the two-lap condition first to verify the declared short rematch beat and preserved progress.

route_status.proven_scope: The assigned probe passed in one isolated Godot 4.7.2-stable headless invocation. Source also defines the three phase career sequence and a Cloud Movie Lounge room/portal.

The internal completion checks do not exercise the target-contract case where the imp finishes first and the contest restarts.

code_constants.scope: Code timers; children may tap at their own pace and no visual frame timing was measured.

code_constants.scope: Source timer, not an observed activity duration.

code_constants.scope: Progress units/configuration, not seconds. This review did not measure child completion time.

tactile.target_size: OperaWorldHotspot2D enforces a minimum 112×112 canvas-pixel invitation hit target; probe checks Magician TRACK and ROPE hit size, clipping and object overlap (scripts/opera_world_hotspot_2d.gd:12-14, 43-47; scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:738-743). The TRACK surface draws three 54-pixel-radius choice circles (108-pixel diameter) while input maps x-position into one of three lanes (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1405-1411, 2849-2855). Neither actual screen scale nor hand/thumb target alignment was rendered or touched in this run.
tactile.press_response: A correct lane press emits a choice gesture; the world advances the target, calls start_shuffle, and redraws. The test log confirms the resulting state and fresh shuffle after accepted hats (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1249-1260, 2849-2855; scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:3536-3548; probe log lines 717-720). The probe did not verify visible response within two rendered frames or actual contact/sound.
tactile.drag_hold_release: TRACK is a one-finger tap into one of three lanes. ROPE is a held one-finger drag along the authored arch from x=16% to x=84% of its surface; trace points outside its corridor, reverse movement, or a progress jump over 18% trigger a 0.24-second rehint and zero progress for that segment (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1676-1687, 1728-1777). Lifting ends the trace; incomplete progress returns to its demonstration state (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1234-1247). These thresholds come from code, not observed child input.
tactile.ownership: The shared gesture surface records one active touch index, ignores another press while held, routes drag only from the active index, and releases that owner's touch (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1249-1278). This source path was not exercised with physical fingers or a Magician-specific multi-touch assertion in this session.
tactile.cancellation: An incomplete ROPE lift resets its demo presentation while retaining the surface's trace progress; the tested assignment did not exercise app focus loss, pause, route cancellation, or interruption during Roshan's approach (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1234-1247; scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:1991-2028).

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: TRACK asks the child to follow a moving hat and choose a lane, then ROPE changes the verb to tracing a visible path. The two mechanics offer distinct agency, but the probe proves only state changes and not whether a child understands that the correct hat is the one to follow.
play_appeal.variety: Magician's room path includes hold, choice, trace, cabinet swipe, and circle phases (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:187-193); the assigned evidence specifically checks TRACK and ROPE. Whether these feel like satisfying different tricks rather than a series of abstract progress bars needs rendered/child observation.
play_appeal.world_response: Accepted TRACK answers move the answer cue through a visible shuffle; authored ROPE tracing moves along an arch and updates trace fill. Real hand-to-rope contact and transformation into the promised ribbon were not seen in this headless run (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5261-5284, 1676-1777; scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:3518-3521).
play_appeal.replay: The phase route offers later cabinet and portal actions after rope, but the session did not reach or exit/re-enter the visible career route. A child's reason to replay TRACK/ROPE remains unknown.
play_appeal.concrete_test_or_proposal: In a short, consented Lenovo Tab M11 observation, show the ordinary Opera Hall route without coaching and note whether the child chooses the Magician portal, follows the moving TRACK hat through several shuffles, and begins ROPE from its indicated start. Test one deliberate wrong-lane tap and one coarse or reverse trace movement; record whether the current cue makes the retry obvious or the child loses the rope. Ask whether they want to repeat one trick, without suggesting the answer. If typical tracing repeatedly restarts, prototype a visibly broad corridor or forgiving resume-from-nearest-point on existing art and compare comprehension and missed-touch counts with this exact current candidate; do not alter protected voice files or treat the proposal as an accepted change.

route_status.proven_scope: The exact Godot 4.7.2-stable probe_opera_2d ran once with an isolated profile and returned OPERA2D|result: ALL OK. The source maps Magician TRACK to pearl_tide_pool and ROPE to teal_shell_stage; probe log checks the phase invitation art/glow/touch target for clipping and Roshan overlap, and checks that correct TRACK choices advance the target and start a fresh shuffle.

The 112-pixel room invitation minimum and scripted state assertions do not establish Mobile composition, physical M11 touch tolerance, frame pacing, comprehension, fun, exact voice match/listening, or owner acceptance. Probe wall time is not gameplay duration. The approved run is for current source/runtime only; external and visual acceptance stays pending under MA-OPERA-004 and MA-OPERA-012. play_sequence.input: Open the Nursery catch task through its visible room/station route; listen to Faron's instruction and look for the cradle and falling baby.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for the task cue to finish and for the first baby to become visible; this review did not measure cue or spawn time.
play_sequence.basis: The active catch phase tells the child to slide the cradle under five falling babies and says pillows keep misses safe (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:336-341); phase prompt uses the active voice/cue (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:2746-2785).

play_sequence.input: Press in the catch area under the baby, then keep a finger moving in a short drag as the baby descends; reposition the cradle if its lane changes.
play_sequence.wait: A press/drag refreshes a 2-second input window. The probe's repeated 0.12-second steering is not a child cadence; watch whether the child naturally refreshes input near the catch band.
play_sequence.basis: Input mapping and timer are in scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:89-127; catch only evaluates while input_live_t is positive at y≥0.74 (scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:172-203).

play_sequence.input: Keep the cradle under the baby through the lower catch band and observe the baby settle into the cradle.
play_sequence.wait: The source catch band spans normalized y=0.74–0.91. At initial speed, the calculated interval is about 0.83 simulated seconds; actual on-screen duration is unmeasured.
play_sequence.basis: Thresholds and catch state are scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:20-21, 192-203; retained caught babies are drawn at :284-291.

play_sequence.input: If a baby lands on the pillows, let the child see the safe landing and try moving the cradle for the next baby.
play_sequence.wait: Allow the miss feedback to appear; its safe-landing entry lasts 1.25 source seconds and fades near the end (scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:161-170, 248-255). Do not treat this as a measured device duration.
play_sequence.basis: The probe deliberately waits without input until at least two misses, confirms no automatic catch and confirms the phase stays active (scripts/probe_opera_nursery.gd:82-89).

play_sequence.input: After two misses, continue steering toward the next baby's lane rather than waiting for a catch to happen automatically.
play_sequence.wait: Observe how the altered lane/speed feels; no fixed child wait is prescribed. Mercy remains active and still requires fresh touch.
play_sequence.basis: After two misses the spawn lane moves near the catcher with an alternating offset and reduced speed (scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:131-149); the probe catches five only after calling steer_to throughout its loop (scripts/probe_opera_nursery.gd:91-103).

play_sequence.input: Let the child respond to the two falling babies that can overlap after early catches, using the single cradle movement to prioritize the lower one.
play_sequence.wait: Observe one drop/catch cycle before prompting; no simultaneous-faller comprehension or pacing was established by the probe.
play_sequence.basis: At two catches, up to two fallers may coexist (scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:178-181); lowest_baby_x returns the largest y (scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:95-103).

play_sequence.input: After five catches, let the cozy cradle and cooperative curtain call settle, then offer the choice to continue or leave without asking the child to repeat.
play_sequence.wait: The caller holds the completion scene for 0.8 source seconds before phase advance; this is a code value, not a rendered/device measurement (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:3685-3689).
play_sequence.basis: The probe checks five catches, cooperative win, cozy-babies cheer and touch-layer restoration on exit (scripts/probe_opera_nursery.gd:102-103, 154-168).

code_constants.value: A press or drag refreshes input_live_t for 2.0 seconds; the catch surface accepts screen press and drag events (scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:22, 89-92, 106-127).
code_constants.scope: Source timer and event handling; not measured device responsiveness.

code_constants.value: Babies catch at normalized y=0.74 and miss at y=0.91; initial fall speed is 0.205 normalized screen heights per simulated second and bottoms at 0.115 (scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:20-21, 139-148, 192-203).
code_constants.scope: The initial interval between catch and pillow thresholds is about 0.83 simulated seconds (0.17/0.205); at the speed floor it is about 1.48 seconds (0.17/0.115). These are calculations from code, not rendered timings.

code_constants.value: The assigned probe advances catch physics in 0.12-second steps and steers to the lowest faller on every iteration (scripts/probe_opera_nursery.gd:91-96).
code_constants.scope: Scripted helper cadence; it does not model a child's finger motion or event cadence.

code_constants.value: After two misses, subsequent drops steer to 0.035–0.11 normalized units from the catcher, their speed is reduced by 0.011 per miss down to 0.115, and catch width grows by 0.013 per miss up to 0.22 (scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:131-148, 192).
code_constants.scope: Code-defined mercy; visual ease and perceived difficulty were not observed.

timing.assumptions: No child-paced duration was observed. The receipt records 10.174 seconds of probe process time, not nursery play time.

tactile.target_size: The catch Control is 392×232 canvas pixels in the phase layout and uses MOUSE_FILTER_STOP (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:2871-2876; scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:44-46). Any point in the control maps the cradle's normalized x position, clamped to 0.10–0.90 (scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:89-108). This generous input surface exceeds the 110×110 project target guidance in source dimensions, but visible scale, panel placement, edge alignment and overlap at supported aspects were not rendered or measured on a device.
tactile.press_response: A valid press immediately updates catcher_x/input_live_t and queues redraw; a catch increments progress, updates the phase panel, calls truthful success feedback and bounces both actors (scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:89-92, 152-159; scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:3665-3689). The probe observes state changes only; it does not establish visible response within two rendered frames or sound audibility.
tactile.drag_hold_release: A screen press places the cradle; screen drags continue to reposition it. A release does not clear the 2-second input window, but merely holding still cannot keep that timer fresh (scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:89-92, 110-125). The actual contact band is y=0.74 through y=0.91, after which a miss safely lands. No physical drag, hold, release, or timing tolerance was tested.
tactile.ownership: The catch Control stops mouse-filter propagation and accepts screen press/drag while active (scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:44-46, 110-120). This controller has no local touch-ID owner field; the session did not test concurrent fingers or the surrounding router's ownership in this overlay.
tactile.cancellation: The catch controller does not handle a canceled touch specially; its freshness timer naturally expires after 2 seconds, and stop() deactivates it and clears fallers/safe landings (scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:81-86, 110-127). Actual focus loss, pause, route exit during an owned touch and resume were not exercised by the focused probe.

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: moving a visible cradle under falling babies gives the child a clear caretaker role, and each intentional catch produces saved-in-cradle/actor feedback. The probe verifies state causality, not that the child reads the falling trajectory or the mercy cue.
play_appeal.variety: For this focus, babies sway, lanes vary, and two can fall simultaneously after two catches (scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:131-149, 172-191). Those changes may make the task lively; their readability and whether simultaneous fallers feel fair remain unobserved.
play_appeal.world_response: Catches retain a baby visibly in the shared cradle and trigger progress/actor response; misses display a briefly fading safe landing, bounce Faron and queue her miss cue (scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:152-169, 241-255, 284-291; scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:3665-3701). The probe asserts safe state/phase progression and exact cue path, not rendered acting or audible playback.
play_appeal.replay: The focused probe proves this catch phase can complete after misses and continue to FEED, but does not test a visible ordinary replay/return route or whether the child wants another round.
play_appeal.concrete_test_or_proposal: On a consented Lenovo Tab M11 session, enter through the ordinary Nursery route and offer no timing coaching. Observe whether the child learns to slide the cradle with the falling baby and continues finger movement/repositioning near contact, whether a short early tap is mistaken for a complete catch, how two simultaneous babies are handled, and whether the pillow-safe miss plus Faron's response invites an independent retry. Record accidental misses, actual touch response and the child's own words/actions; do not infer appeal from this scripted probe.

route_status.proven_scope: The exact Godot 4.7.2-stable probe ran once with an isolated profile and reported NURSERY result ALL OK. Source tracing shows the live career route creates OperaNurseryCatch for Nursery, shows it for CATCH BABIES, and sizes it to the activity surface (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:1337-1345, 2654-2686, 2873-2877). The probe proves no-input misses, safe landings, post-miss mercy and five catches after its scripted steering sequence.
route_status.route_gaps: The probe instantiates the act directly, opens the catch task through _open_armed_task, and calls steer_to/._process rather than navigating a fresh-save Castle route or injecting ordinary screen-touch/drag events (scripts/probe_opera_nursery.gd:11-41, 62-96, 180-184). Headless rendering is not Mobile visual evidence. No physical touch, Lenovo Tab M11 latency/frame pacing, child comprehension/appeal, or owner acceptance was observed. play_sequence.input: From the visible Opera Hall route, choose Pop Star and enter the lesson; do not assume the probe's direct setup proves this route.
play_sequence.wait: Allow the welcome cue and arrival to finish before touching the lesson surface.
play_sequence.basis: Opera Hall lists Pop Star among its three venue careers (scripts/opera_house.gd:120-123); venue route remains unobserved here.

play_sequence.input: Complete the Pop Star practice phases using the visible prompt: hold the microphone, tap the glowing dance arrow, then tap the noisy band when cued.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for each current phase cue and its response before the next input; no duration estimate is asserted.
play_sequence.basis: Practice phase definitions and instructions are scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:229-235.

play_sequence.input: At RHYTHM, keep hands still while the first two-star phrase plays.
play_sequence.wait: Wait through the shown phrase and for the listening cue; notes are scheduled 0.55 seconds apart (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5877-5892). This is code timing, not measured play cadence.
play_sequence.basis: Echo SHOW mode lights notes before listening; scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5880-5892.

play_sequence.input: Tap the two lit stars in order, then wait and tap the three-star phrase in order.
play_sequence.wait: After each completed phrase, wait for the next phrase to begin; code uses 0.7 seconds (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5917-5923).
play_sequence.basis: Verse arrays [0,2] and [0,1,2], with correct taps advancing one note at a time (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:114,5907-5925).

play_sequence.input: Wait for the final reversed phrase, then tap its notes in the displayed/sung order.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for the listening cue before each answer; no real-time measurement was made.
play_sequence.basis: The final source verse is [2,1,0] and the probe's focused echo checkpoint leg restores the first note before accepting the second (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:114; scripts/probe_opera_performance.gd:303-343).

play_sequence.input: If a note is missed, wait for the stars to replay and try the phrase again; do not coach the child during the observation.
play_sequence.wait: Code replays a missed verse after 0.9 seconds (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5923-5929); this is not observed child pacing.
play_sequence.basis: Wrong-note path restarts the verse without a fail state (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5923-5929).

play_sequence.input: After RHYTHM completes, follow the ENCORE cue by drawing one big circle, then let the child choose whether to replay or leave.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for the phase result and choice; no total duration or reward timing is claimed.
play_sequence.basis: Stage RHYTHM and ENCORE have echo/circle modes and short verbal cues (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:343-347).

code_constants.value: Echo shows the next note after a 0.55-second interval; after a completed verse it waits 0.7 seconds before replaying the next verse, and a wrong note waits 0.9 seconds before replay (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5880-5892,5917-5929).
code_constants.scope: Source intervals only; no child-visible cadence or rendered timing was observed.

code_constants.value: Echo verses grow through [0,2], [0,1,2], and [2,1,0] (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:114).
code_constants.scope: Three coded rounds; not a measure of total play time.

timing.assumptions: No gameplay time was observed. Isolated probe wall time does not measure a play session.

tactile.target_size: Echo stars are centered at 22%, 50%, and 78% of surface width and 52% of height; drawing uses 54-pixel radius (64 while lit), with nearest-star acceptance only within 92 pixels (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5865,5894-5905,5950-5958). Actual screen projection, target separation and hit alignment on Lenovo Tab M11 are unknown.
tactile.press_response: During listening, a correct tap lights the selected star and advances input; a wrong star asks the stars to replay (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5906-5929). The assigned probe did not establish visible response latency or voice playback.
tactile.drag_hold_release: Echo is discrete press/tap input; no drag or hold is required in _echo_press (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5894-5931). Release behavior and ordinary GUI event routing were not established by the assigned headless run.
tactile.ownership: The mechanic is tap-based and this review found no focused assertion establishing multi-touch ownership for echo. One-finger live input is the expected route, but no physical touch was tried.
tactile.cancellation: No focused echo cancellation, pause, focus-loss, or re-entry behavior was verified in this invocation.

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: listening to a short star phrase and choosing its notes gives a preschooler a clear listen-then-answer role, with no punishment on a wrong answer. Whether the cue is understandable without coaching remains unobserved.
play_appeal.variety: The three verses change from two notes to three, then reverse order; the following encore changes the verb to drawing a circle (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:114; scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:343-347). This is source variety, not observed child interest.
play_appeal.world_response: Correct notes produce a star glow and the assembled-song row grows after each verse; a wrong note restarts the phrase instead of ending play (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5907-5929,5950-5965). The probe log does not establish how readable or encouraging this looks or sounds on device.
play_appeal.replay: The source repeats a missed verse and then offers the encore phase. Hypothesis: the replay may feel supportive if the child notices the glowing cue; observed replay choice is absent.
play_appeal.concrete_test_or_proposal: In a short consented child observation, play one verse without coaching, then allow a wrong tap and one retry. Record whether the child waits for the stars, taps the lit sequence, notices the replay after a miss, and independently chooses to continue to the encore. If the wait feels inert, test a more apparent visual countdown/glow cadence while keeping wrong answers harmless and requiring the child's taps for progress.

sessions.focus: Ballerina pose ribbon and twirl input

play_sequence.beat: Enter through the normal Opera House route and choose the Ballerina activity from its visible room trigger; record where Roshan and the activity choice appear.
play_sequence.input: Tap the visible Ballerina trigger once; wait for the room transition and spoken cue to finish.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child identify the activity from its picture/setting without reading or adult direction?

play_sequence.beat: Watch Pearl Mirror show a held pose and moving demonstration cue.
play_sequence.input: No touch for the 2.15-second pose demonstration and its voice handoff; then wait one second.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child watch Roshan, then look toward a matching portrait?

play_sequence.beat: Choose each matching mirror portrait and watch the pose phrase change position.
play_sequence.input: Tap one portrait, lift fully, wait through the next 2.15-second demo, then tap the matching portrait; repeat for all three rounds.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does changing portrait position sustain attention, and does the child visibly enjoy Roshan's pose changes?

play_sequence.beat: Trace the luminous Ribbon Trail from its pearl along the S current.
play_sequence.input: Wait 1.55 seconds for the demo, press the highlighted start pearl, drag along the curve in short strokes, lift near halfway, wait through the 1.55-second replay, then press the new pearl and continue.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child treat the glowing trail as a path and choose to continue after lifting?

play_sequence.beat: Perform Grand Twirl around the shell music box.
play_sequence.input: Wait 1.55 seconds for the demo, press the pearl handle on the ring, drag around the ring in a comfortable direction, lift around halfway, wait through the replay, then press the moved handle and continue in the same direction.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child imitate the demonstrated turn and notice Roshan's pose cue changes?

play_sequence.beat: Finish the recital and observe the return/replay choice.
play_sequence.input: Release after the final twirl sector; wait for completion response and one second before touching any visible exit/replay control.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child request another act or recital on their own, or leave calmly without adult help?

source_constants.scripts/opera_ballet_surface.gd:30: first assist after 5 seconds of playable no-progress time
source_constants.scripts/opera_ballet_surface.gd:31: strong assist after 10 seconds of playable no-progress time

estimates: A successful in-game route that completes all acts may take at least the demos plus deliberate input; no total duration is inferable from the internal probe.
The helper's 2.227-second wall time is tool runtime and is not gameplay duration.

tactile.target_size: Probe verifies pose portraits are at least 180x180 at its 854x660 test surface; ribbon resume target is 128x128 base pixels, corridor 116 pixels, twirl ring 116 pixels wide and handle diameter 112 pixels. DL-UI-03's 110x110 threshold is met in these assertions, but phone projection and finger occlusion are untested.
tactile.press_response: Probe confirms a matching portrait banks one round; invalid portrait yields no payout and replays its demo. Ribbon/twirl wrong paths do not pay; positive progress emits gesture feedback. Rendered response latency is not measured.
tactile.drag_hold_release: Ribbon accepts progress along the S curve and keeps monotonic partial progress after release; twirl accepts incremental movement around the ring and preserves partial progress after release. No long press is required.
tactile.ownership: The surface's internal held state gates drags and is cleared on release. This probe directly calls private handlers and cannot establish real pointer ownership, competing fingers, pause/focus cancellation, or hardware sampling.
tactile.cancellation: Lifting mid-ribbon or mid-twirl preserves accepted progress. Probe also checks straight-chord/diameter attempts do not bypass the required path. No real focus-loss cancellation was exercised.

play_appeal.hypothesis: The three-act switch from pose matching to tracing a glowing current to orbiting a shell gives a young player distinct hand actions and visible authorship. The orbit's Roshan pose cues may make the final gesture feel like a performance rather than filling a meter. Repeating the recital could be satisfying if the child notices the held pose phrase and changing direction freedom.
play_appeal.appeal_test: On the intended phone, observe whether the child chooses to repeat a favorite act or asks to perform the recital again without adult prompting; note spontaneous smiles/vocalizations and whether they describe or imitate Roshan's poses. Do not infer appeal from probe completion.

route_status.proven_scope: The existing probe constructed OperaBalletSurface directly at 854x660 and exercised all three supported modes through their internal press/drag/release methods. It did not enter the Opera House or prove the child-visible Ballerina route.
route_gaps: child comprehension, enjoyment, and session length

play_sequence.beat: Find the Candy Maker workshop from its normal Castle-room invitation and approach COAT STRAWBERRIES.
play_sequence.input: Tap the visible Candy Maker trigger once; wait for Roshan's walk and object-opening flourish, then wait for the spoken cue to finish before touching the activity.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child connect the strawberry/candy setting with the invitation and wait for Roshan to arrive?

play_sequence.beat: Coat the five berries with syrup and see their color/state change.
play_sequence.input: Wait for the cue; press and hold the ladle, keep the stream over the berries, and lift once the visual brim/completion response occurs. Wait about one second for the ladle to settle and the next station invitation.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child notice the berries becoming coated and understand why the task changed?

play_sequence.beat: Sort the same berries into matching color/shape lanes.
play_sequence.input: Tap the taffy-press invitation; wait through travel, opening, and cue. Press the moving berry, drag it into a matching lane, and release; repeat for each prompted piece. If a wrong drop happens, wait for the returned piece and demonstration before retrying.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child use color or silhouette matching intentionally and treat a returned piece as a retry rather than a failure?

play_sequence.beat: Glaze the sorted berries with a circular motion.
play_sequence.input: Tap the cottage invitation and wait for arrival/opening/cue. Draw comfortable circles over the candy; lift between attempts if desired and wait for the next hint before resuming. Wait one second after the accepted completion.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the circular gesture feel distinct from sorting, and does the berry/cake visual make the glaze payoff clear?

play_sequence.beat: Place each finished strawberry on the actual cake.
play_sequence.input: Tap the cart invitation; wait for travel/opening/cue. Tap the indicated candy and cake placement anchors one at a time, lifting between taps; after the fifth placement wait for the completed cake reveal to finish.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child see that each tap decorates the same cake and show interest in the finished result?

play_sequence.beat: Offer the normal exit/return and observe whether the child wants another activity or another Candy Maker run.
play_sequence.input: Wait two seconds after the cake result, then make no suggestion; let the child tap a visible exit/return or replay choice if present and wait for the room to settle.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child independently choose what to do next or request the Candy Maker again?

play_appeal.hypothesis: Coating, matching, circling, and placing the same five strawberries on the actual cake offer a clear hand-action change while keeping one ingredient and the cake's result in view. The proposed appeal depends on whether the child notices that each action changes those same berries and chooses to continue to decorate the cake; a four-step task could also feel repetitive if the visual changes are too subtle.
play_appeal.appeal_test: On the intended phone, give a child the normal spoken/pictorial invitation without naming the gestures. Observe whether they independently switch from pouring to dragging, circling, and tapping, notice the strawberries becoming cake decorations, and ask to continue or replay. Record confusion, adult prompts, and voluntary replay without converting these observations into a numeric fun score.

These are scripted engine assertions, not a fresh-save visible GUI/device traversal. The current Chapter Two adapter separately defines COAT, SORT, GLAZE, and PLACE ON CAKE; this probe does not sequence those four story phases end to end.

sessions.focus: Chef stirring and changing physical states

play_sequence.beat: Find the Chef invitation in the normal Castle kitchen route and reach the mixing bowl.
play_sequence.input: Tap the visible bowl invitation once; wait for Roshan to finish walking and the station opening, then wait for the MIX voice cue before touching the bowl.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child identify the bowl as the next place to act and wait for Roshan to arrive?
play_sequence.basis: scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:1894-1911 maps Chef phases to stations and :1991-2028 separates approach from task opening.

play_sequence.beat: Pour the ingredients into the mixing bowl.
play_sequence.input: On the spoken/pictorial MIX cue, press and hold the pitcher control so the stream reaches the bowl; lift when the batter reaches its visible completed state, then wait for the completion picture and next phase invitation.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child see the bowl fill and connect the pour with the new batter state?

play_sequence.beat: Stir the batter with the whisk.
play_sequence.input: Wait for the STIR cue; press on the bowl surface and keep one finger down while drawing broad circles around the bowl center in one direction. Continue until the stirred swirl appears; then lift and wait for the next cue.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the whisk follow the finger clearly, and does the child notice that the batter changed because of the circles?
play_sequence.basis: scripts/chapter_two_career_scene_adapter.gd:23; scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1191-1207; scripts/opera_chef_surface.gd:90-103.

play_sequence.beat: Bake the batter and take the golden cake out.
play_sequence.input: Wait for the oven cue and visual golden state; tap or press the mitt when invited, release, and wait for the baked tiers to appear and the next invitation.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child wait for the oven state before reaching for the mitt?
play_sequence.basis: scripts/chapter_two_career_scene_adapter.gd:24 and scripts/opera_chef_surface.gd:104-107.

play_sequence.beat: Stack the cake tiers.
play_sequence.input: Wait for the STACK cue; tap each visible tier/placement anchor one at a time, lifting between taps. Wait for the completed cake to settle before the frosting cue.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child understand that each placement builds the same cake rather than selecting an unrelated object?
play_sequence.basis: scripts/chapter_two_career_scene_adapter.gd:25; scripts/opera_chef_surface.gd:109,124-151.

The probe checks room hotspot bounds and that the one room interaction layer exists, but does not measure its projection on a phone or the child's finger occlusion; DL-UI-03 reach/compliance remains unverified.

That links hand movement to a food state and could make the next baking action feel like a consequence of the child's work. It may be satisfying if the bowl change is easy to notice; repeated circle drawing could also feel like meter-filling if the batter's visible state does not change during the gesture.
play_appeal.appeal_test: On the intended phone, use the normal spoken and pictorial route without naming the motion. Observe whether the child discovers the bowl, traces the whisk without adult hand-over-hand help, notices both the moving whisk and finished batter, and chooses to continue into baking or asks to stir again. Record adult prompts, interruptions, and voluntary replay; do not assign a numeric fun score.

sessions.focus: Detective clue intention vs random tapping

play_sequence.beat: Enter Detective from its normal Castle-room invitation and reach the magnifier tower.
play_sequence.input: From a fresh save, use the visible room route. Tap the painted magnifier station once and lift; wait through Roshan authored walk and missing-crown/search voice sequence before touching the lens.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child recognize the station as the start of a search and wait to see what the magnifier does?

play_sequence.beat: Follow the wordless lens demonstration toward its first clue.
play_sequence.input: After the spoken cue, make no input for about two seconds while the demo moves; then touch down and drag the magnifier toward the indicated glint. Stop over it and wait at least half a second for a response.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child notice that the demonstration points to a clue without automatically completing it?

play_sequence.beat: Inspect one ordinary room detail, then deliberately return to a clue.
play_sequence.input: Drag the lens across one ordinary prop and lift; wait one second for its pulse/chime to finish. Then drag to a glint, stop the lens there for about half a second, and lift.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Can the child distinguish an optional prop reaction from a clue-found response and follow the resulting trail?

play_sequence.beat: Follow successive light trails through the required clue search.
play_sequence.input: After each clue-found line, wait for the trail to appear, drag toward its endpoint, and stop over the next clue for about half a second. Lift between sweeps; repeat until the in-game search goal advances.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child use the trail as a helpful next-step cue, and do the repeated search gestures remain interesting?

play_sequence.beat: Wait for the delayed hint if the child pauses or loses the clue.
play_sequence.input: When the lens has not found a clue, leave it alone and wait up to about twelve seconds; if the glint appears, give no extra verbal instruction and let the child drag the lens to it and pause.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the glint arrive soon enough to help without making the child feel the game solved the clue for them?

play_sequence.beat: After the search result settles, observe the child next choice.
play_sequence.input: Wait two seconds after the success response and trail settle, then make no adult suggestion. Let the child use the visible in-game continuation, room return, or replay option if presented.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child choose to continue the mystery, explore another detail, or ask to replay?

tactile.drag_hold_release: The intended gesture is one-finger sweep/drag, then keeping the glass centered on a clue for 0.45 seconds; source exposes a dwell progress arc (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:4451-4476, 4576). tactile.ownership: The assigned probe validates its scripted route and internal clue state, not actual pointer ownership. The source handles screen-touch and screen-drag events, but no second-finger arbitration or touch-router interaction is asserted by this probe.
tactile.cancellation: The probe calls act.cancel() during teardown (scripts/probe_opera_detective.gd:136-137), but does not interrupt a real drag, pause/focus-loss, or verify post-cancel lens state. These recovery paths remain unobserved here.

play_appeal.hypothesis: The lens makes searching a painted room feel like an active investigation: the child can sweep freely, inspect non-clue details, then follow a light trail to the next clue. Separate clue, case-board, and spotlight tasks may keep the story moving, but repeated fixed dwell searches could start to feel like scanning rather than discovery.
play_appeal.appeal_test: On the intended phone, let a child hear the normal voice cue and watch the initial demonstration without naming the control. Observe whether they independently move the lens, pause over a glint, follow the next trail, and distinguish optional prop reactions from clue progress. After the three clue-search steps and transition to the case board, record adult prompts, accidental clue finds, visible delight/frustration, and whether the child asks to continue or replay; do not assign a numeric fun score.
