play_sequence.status: Proposed acceptance script; not performed as visible or child play. The probe internally covers the mask/button steps only.
beats: From a fresh Chapter Two save after the prior story gate, use the visible Family Dining Room Farmer route and wait for the first task cue. Record whether a physical room object can open GATHER STRAWBERRIES; code has no Farmer station for that phase (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:1902-1911,2497-2524).

If the room is waiting, give it exactly 9 seconds with no input; check the repeated phase prompt/demo, then continue to exactly 20 seconds and check the auto-walk assist. The source only invokes that assist when an armed station exists (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:4622-4638).

After a valid visible task entry is available, make one ordinary tap on each of three different visible berries, with no hold or drag; pause/leave and reload at 3/5. The probe's mask-3 case is simulated rather than saved through these actions (probe.gd:94-120).
Re-enter and make one tap on the next berry; verify it alone is enabled before tapping and becomes disabled/dim immediately afterward (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:1014-1055; probe.gd:105-119).

Tap the final fifth berry once; wait 1.1 seconds for the authored completion timer and inspect that the saved mask is 0x1F and the next phase has a visible, reachable entry (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:1057-1062).

Concrete appeal test on the target phone: without adult instruction, observe whether the child chooses and taps the next berry, recovers after resuming 3/5, recognizes what changed, and voluntarily continues toward basket delivery; record any missed target, waiting, help request, or decision to stop.

code_constants: The Farmer pickup completion sets phase_complete_t=1.1 seconds after the fifth pick (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:1057-1062).

While waiting in a closed room, the phase prompt is repeated at idle_t >= 9 seconds; at idle_t >= 20 seconds the code attempts to walk to the armed station (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:4622-4638).
Chapter Two normal-phase transition uses a 1.0-second phase_gap after phase 0; subsequent phase arming keeps the room open for discovery (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:2460-2468,3615-3617).
timing.assumptions: These are source timers, not observed child-session durations. The 20-second assist only calls the hotspot route if armed_station resolves; Farmer's missing room-object warnings leave this condition unproven and the code path has no station for the cited phases. Probe wall time (14.874 seconds) is execution time only.

tactile.ownership: The probe uses one signal emission per remaining pick and checks a duplicate next-button emission earns no additional credit (probe.log:10-26). It does not test touch IDs, simultaneous fingers, or GUI routing.
tactile.cancellation: Partial pickup state is checked after direct mask initialization, not after an actual pause, activity exit, focus loss, save write, or app restart. Those lifecycle paths remain unverified here.

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: five separated, large berry targets and only one enabled next pick could make the gathering goal concrete and support choosing a target. The actual target art, focus, pointer, speech, and response were not viewed or heard.
play_appeal.variety: The reviewed Farmer gather beat is five object taps; this probe does not review the later Farmer garden/lawn activity, so variety beyond harvesting is unknown.
play_appeal.world_response: In the asserted setup, each pick increments persistent mask progress, dims/disables the selected berry, and the fifth sets phase advance pending; no visible capture verifies the response in context.
play_appeal.replay: The resume cases suggest the child can continue at the next uncollected berry after interruption, but interruption/re-entry was simulated by assigning saved masks, not performed through a user route. Child appeal and willingness to repeat remain hypotheses.

Probe log ends RESULT: PASS failures=0.

play_sequence.beat: Ordinary-entry and first contact
play_sequence.input: On an isolated test profile, enter Doctor through the normal Castle room route; let the Doctor room and its spoken/pointer cue appear, then tap the one currently glowing treatment object once.
play_sequence.wait: Wait until Roshan reaches the authored approach and the hotspot opening completes; source has no fixed travel duration, so do not infer one.
play_sequence.expected: The chosen station opens the current phase; unrelated room taps do not skip the physical station route.

play_sequence.beat: Wash
play_sequence.input: Press and continuously hold one finger on the bubbly basin for 3.6 seconds in the Chapter Two story phase; keep the same finger down until the wash completes.
play_sequence.wait: After completion, leave the result visible for 2.2 seconds. Allow the next phase's 1.0-second between-phase gap; the finale-entry gap is 2.6 seconds when CAST begins at finale_start 3.
play_sequence.expected: Held-time progress reaches WASH's 3.6 goal, then advances to FIND after the result hold.

play_sequence.beat: Find the sore plush
play_sequence.input: Tap the currently glowing patient choice four times, waiting for the refreshed cue after each correct choice; do not drum on the screen.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for the phase to open and for each choice reflash; after the fourth accepted choice, wait 2.2 seconds for the completion picture.
play_sequence.expected: FIND's story goal is four; a correct choice updates the target, while a wrong choice retains and reflashes the same answer.

play_sequence.beat: Scan the X-ray
play_sequence.input: Touch the scanner, drag one continuous finger segment through the first sore spot at normalized surface point (0.65, 0.50), then the next at (0.48, 0.40), and release. If the child lifts early, allow the demonstration to replay and continue from the remaining spot.
play_sequence.wait: Allow the 2.2-second completion-picture hold after both spots register. Before CAST, allow the 2.6-second finale-entry gap coded for phase index 3.
play_sequence.expected: The scanner reveals two spots in order; each qualifying segment earns one X-ray unit and an incomplete release preserves found progress.

play_sequence.beat: Wrap the cast and test appeal
play_sequence.input: Draw two full circles with one finger over the cast surface, following the Doctor's demonstration, then allow the story result to settle. Observe without coaching whether the child anticipates the next step, recognizes the plush is treated, and chooses to replay or leave.
play_sequence.wait: Hold the completed cast picture for 2.2 seconds. For an appeal check, offer one voluntary replay after the final result; do not require an adult prompt or measure duration from the probe runner.
play_sequence.expected: CAST reaches the story goal of 2.0 circle units and completes the four-phase story treatment. Free-play BANDAGE is a separate additional mechanic and should be assessed only on that route.

source_constants.value: Chapter Two Doctor phase goals: WASH 3.6, FIND 4.0, X-RAY 2.0, CAST 2.0; this story adapter ends after CAST.
Free-play Doctor treatment goals include WASH 4.5, FIND 6.0, X-RAY 3.0, CAST 3.6, BANDAGE 6.5; the broader seven-phase list also includes two imp encounters.
Each completed phase holds its finished picture for 2.2 seconds; phase-advance timing is distinct from the goal-work time.
Doctor X-ray has two ordered scan spots.

Gesture goals are abstract progress units except the Doctor hold, which accumulates elapsed held time in the career-world tick (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:4658-4667); hand travel and touch latency are not measured.

tactile.target_size: The probe asserts Doctor station hit regions meet 110×110 base-canvas pixels and that hotspots remain in bounds and clear Roshan's idle body (scripts/probe_opera_diegetic_paths.gd:222-273,300-324). This is table-level geometry; device projection and visual prominence were not measured.
tactile.press_response: Source routes a press on the currently armed hotspot through the approved station path, then opens the phase after the hotspot opening finishes (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:1991-2029). No visible routed press was exercised. X-ray feedback code lights a found spot and emits one unit of progress on a qualifying scan segment (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:4290-4316).

play_appeal.hypothesis: The ordered care sequence could feel varied because it changes from a sustained wash to a choice, a two-point scan, and a circular cast. The progress is tied to different gestures rather than passive waiting. Whether the patient cues are noticeable, the order makes sense to a preschooler, or the repeated hand motions stay enjoyable is unobserved.

sessions.focus: Painter pictured creativity and repeat value

play_sequence.beat: Reach the easel
play_sequence.input: From a fresh test save that can reach the Painter room, let Roshan's room cue finish, then tap the currently invited easel once. Do not tap the painting remotely while she is walking.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for authored approach and the object-opening flourish; source does not give a fixed travel duration.
play_sequence.expected: The PAINT hotspot opens the phase only after arrival; the probe asserts the hotspot starts a route and not immediate progress (runtime log lines 826-828, 848-854).

play_sequence.beat: Reveal the sunrise
play_sequence.input: Press inside the cloudy square and drag one finger in broad horizontal and vertical passes until the underlying picture is clear; lift after each pass and continue from remaining cloudy regions if needed.
play_sequence.wait: No fixed stroke duration. After the phase completes, let the finished picture hold for 2.2 seconds; allow the 2.6-second finale-entry gap when GALLERY is next.
play_sequence.expected: Only new crossed cells count; a stationary press does not fill the board. At 38 of 60 cells the sunrise reveal completes.

play_sequence.beat: Choose five finishing stamps
play_sequence.input: Tap five separated places of your choice on the stamp surface, waiting for each stamp to appear before the next tap.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for each visual response, then allow the 2.2-second completed-picture hold and the 2.6-second finale-entry gap.
play_sequence.expected: All five stamps can be placed by the child; the runtime probe confirms stamp coordinates are not forced to authored anchors (log line 816).

play_sequence.beat: Hang the picture
play_sequence.input: Tap the one glowing gallery frame once to hang the sunrise; wait for the chosen-frame response rather than tapping repeatedly.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for the selection cue and completed result to settle; no additional fixed hang duration is established by this review.
play_sequence.expected: The gallery choice ends the painting sequence with the selected frame cue; source maps GALLERY to choice and goal 1.0.

play_sequence.beat: Check agency and repeat appeal
play_sequence.input: Without suggesting another turn, observe whether the child points out a mark they chose, asks to repaint/stamp again, or leaves. If they choose replay, offer the route again and let them place the five stamps differently.
play_sequence.wait: Allow the child to finish their thought or leave at their own pace; do not use runner wall time as session length.
play_sequence.expected: Record whether the child can explain/show a personal choice and initiates replay without adult prompting. This is a proposed child acceptance check, not evidence from L29.

source_constants.value: Stage PAINT goal 1.0, STAMPS goal 5.0, GALLERY goal 1.0; the source strings voice a sunrise reveal, five free stamps, and choosing a frame.
Paint reveal uses a 10 by 6 grid with 0.62 required coverage; _paint_required_cells rounds this to 38 cells. The drag brush marks a cross of up to five cells per sample.

A completed generic surface phase keeps its result for 2.2 seconds. Non-final phase transition gap is 1.0 seconds; entering the finale is 2.6 seconds (Painter stage has three phases and GALLERY is last).

timing.assumptions: No gameplay duration is inferred. The helper wall time was about 43 seconds and is probe execution only. Paint stroke time, travel/arrival, spoken line length, touch latency, and voluntary replay are unmeasured. Wait only for the authored cue/state to finish where no fixed travel duration is given.

tactile.target_size: The internal probe asserts each Painter PAINT/STAMPS/GALLERY hotspot art, glow and touch target do not clip and remain clear of Roshan (probe_opera_2d.gd assertions reflected in runtime log lines 826-834). It does not report projected hit dimensions on the target phone. Paint canvas is a centered square bounded by 46% of surface width and 72% of surface height (opera_gesture_surface.gd:4714-4718).
tactile.press_response: Code begins paint only on a press inside the canvas; a drag across new cells gives brief positive feedback and signals completion when 38 of 60 cells are covered (opera_gesture_surface.gd:4730-4732,4762-4787). No real routed stroke ran in L29.
tactile.drag_hold_release: Paint is drag-based; a stationary press adds no coverage, and release clears paint_dragging (opera_gesture_surface.gd:4762-4791). The grid-spaced interpolation should prevent gaps in quick drags by code inspection, not measured touch testing.
tactile.ownership: The generic surface records the active touch index and ignores foreign presses/drags while held (opera_gesture_surface.gd:1249-1267). The probe's Painter room checks include foreign-finger rejection during approach (runtime log line 842); no physical multitouch behavior was measured.
tactile.cancellation: The room probe checks canceling a pending touch clears movement/action (runtime log line 844). It does not test canceling an in-progress paint stroke, pause/focus loss during paint, or lifecycle re-entry after a partially revealed image.

play_appeal.hypothesis: A cloudy veil that visibly gives way to a sunrise could make the child's own hand motion feel consequential, and unrestricted stamp placement leaves room for personal choices. A second play may feel different if the child changes where stamps go. The current code fixes the revealed picture and the five-stamp count, so repeat value depends on whether placement and the celebration feel expressive enough; neither child delight nor a desire to replay was observed.

Painter-specific checks cover Canvas setup, three stage hotspot bindings and geometry, passive-safe approach/opening, free-position STAMPS, phase completion lifecycle, and exit cleanup (probe log lines 796-868).

play_sequence.beat: Enter the Astronaut pipe board
play_sequence.input: From a verified ordinary Astronaut PIPES entry, wait for the spoken instruction, then touch one tray tile once and release.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for the phase instruction to finish; no fixed entry animation duration was established here.
play_sequence.expected: PIPES asks the child to connect fuel tank to rocket across three boards (opera_career_world_2d.gd:205-207,326).

play_sequence.beat: Place a straight pipe
play_sequence.input: Tap the tray tile, lift, then tap the next open cell along the visible route; alternatively drag a tile from tray to an open cell and lift.
play_sequence.wait: After each placement, watch for fuel movement. In an incomplete route the next flow step is scheduled every 1.2 seconds of game time.
play_sequence.expected: The pipe appears in the chosen cell, the tray count drops by one, and fuel advances only through connected matching mouths.

play_sequence.beat: Follow round-one fuel to the rocket
play_sequence.input: Place the two horizontal pieces in cells 5 and 6 as the probe does, using one-finger tap-tap for the first and drag for the second.
play_sequence.wait: Allow about 9 seconds of simulated game time for the probe's round-one path, then wait 1.5 seconds across the board transition; these are probe timing legs, not a measured child pace.
play_sequence.expected: Fuel reaches the rocket, the board completes, and round two appears after the one-second internal pause.

play_sequence.beat: Try and repair a wrong route
play_sequence.input: Place the southwest elbow in cell 0, let fuel reach it, then tap that fueled pipe and release it back over the tray.
play_sequence.wait: Wait about 4 seconds of simulated game time for fuel to reach the bad turn. If left blocked, the cell hint begins at 8 seconds and an eligible wrong pipe returns after 16 seconds.
play_sequence.expected: The pipe lifts, fuel drains back to the last connected segment, and the tile returns to the tray without losing the round.

play_sequence.beat: Complete the second route around the sleeping imp
play_sequence.input: Place SE at cell 0, H at 1, SW at 2, and NE at 6, as in the focused probe; let the child observe the fuel and imp response.
play_sequence.wait: The probe allocates 14 seconds of simulated flow time. Once the route is complete, flow steps use 0.35 seconds rather than 1.2 seconds.
play_sequence.expected: Fuel follows the connected turns around the imp and round two completes; the hint must point to a useful cell rather than the imp.

play_sequence.beat: Test the final board and ownership
play_sequence.input: Use the third board's changed exit direction to connect the remaining pieces. During a routed acceptance session, keep one tile held and briefly touch a second tray spot with another finger, then release the first finger.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for the 1-second inter-board pause and let fuel advance at the incomplete or complete-path interval as appropriate; do not use a fixed total session duration.
play_sequence.expected: The third route reaches the rocket; a second finger does not steal the carried tile, and each tile remains recoverable.

play_sequence.beat: Check appeal without prompting
play_sequence.input: After the third board response settles, pause and let the child decide whether to show the route, ask to play again, or leave.
play_sequence.wait: Allow the child to finish or leave at their pace; do not treat probe wall time as session duration.
play_sequence.expected: Record whether the child initiates repair, tracks the fuel's causal path, and asks to replay without an adult cue; this is a proposed test, not evidence collected in L30.

source_constants.value: A complete pipe path advances fuel every 0.35 seconds; an incomplete path advances every 1.2 seconds. A blocked flow waits, starts hinting after 8.0 seconds, and returns an eligible wrong pipe after 16.0 seconds of accumulated wait.
Solved boards pause for 1.0 second before the next board is set up. The pipe phase goal is 3.0 boards.

The probe advances simulated surface time in 0.1-second increments and asks for 9.0 seconds of round-one flow, then 1.5 seconds for the inter-board pause; its later recovery legs request 4.0 and 14.0 simulated seconds.

timing.assumptions: No child session duration is estimated. The helper's 0.856-second wall time is probe execution only, not gameplay timing. Source timers measure accumulated game delta; voice duration, travel, touch latency and voluntary replay were not measured.

tactile.target_size: The probe constructs an 852x560 surface and computes cell and tray centers for scripted taps/drags (probe_opera_pipe.gd:19-26,48-52). PIPE_CELL and PIPE_TRAY_SIDE define the actionable geometry, but no rendered or projected dimensions on the Lenovo Tab M11 were measured (opera_gesture_surface.gd:5416-5437).
tactile.press_response: A tray press removes and carries a tile immediately; a tap on an empty cell places the remembered selection, while a drag release on an empty cell places the carried tile (opera_gesture_surface.gd:5562-5573,5603-5610,5613-5633). Placement queues redraw and emits the pipe gesture signal; visible feedback timing was not measured on a rendered device.
tactile.drag_hold_release: One-finger tap-tap and tray-to-cell drag are both supported in source. Releasing a carried tile outside the grid returns it selected to the tray; releasing over an occupied cell restores it to its source cell when applicable (opera_gesture_surface.gd:5613-5633). The probe checks tray-tap/cell-tap, drag, and lift/release paths, not a real finger hold or interrupt.
tactile.ownership: Current _gui_input ignores a new screen press while held and accepts drag/release only for the active touch index (opera_gesture_surface.gd:1249-1267). L30 did not send InputEventScreenTouch through this handler, so this code-level ownership observation needs a routed two-finger acceptance test.
tactile.cancellation: Source returns a carried tile to tray on a release outside the board and allows placed wrong tiles to be lifted, including after fuel reaches them (opera_gesture_surface.gd:5584-5601,5613-5633). No application focus-loss or pause cancellation was exercised by L30.

play_appeal.hypothesis: The fuel visibly traveling through a pipe the child assembled could make the route feel causal, and the sleeping imp and changing exit direction may add variety across boards. Repairing an already-fueled mistake and seeing the route continue may support experimentation. These are source-grounded appeal hypotheses, not observed child reactions.
play_appeal.agency_test: Offer the child an incorrect pipe choice, let them lift or wait for the hint, then observe whether they independently repair the route and attend to the fuel reaching the rocket. After the third board, offer no prompt and record whether they request another turn or leave.

play_sequence.beat: Brush and assemble the fossil
play_sequence.input: Press inside the fossil grid, sweep back and forth across its five rows with one continuous finger, and lift; once three pieces appear, drag each from fossil_piece_home(0..2) to the matching fossil_piece_target(0..2) and lift each there.
play_sequence.wait: Keep brushing until 26 of 40 cells are clear, then wait for the phase to advance after all three release snaps; no fixed duration is established.
play_sequence.expected: Dust clears under the brush and fossil pieces remain recoverable until snapped; each piece accepts release within 92 pixels of its target.

play_sequence.beat: Swish the pan
play_sequence.input: Press the pan center, swipe at least 46 pixels to one side, reverse at least 46 pixels, and continue alternating direction until nine reversals register; then lift.
play_sequence.wait: Observe mineral finds appear as wash progress changes; no timed hold is required by the source.
play_sequence.expected: Pan movement follows the finger, directional reversals wash the pan and reveal up to three minerals, and the task completes on reversal nine.

play_sequence.beat: Tap five geode seams, then pull
play_sequence.input: Tap and lift at each of the five geode_seam_spot indices 0 through 4; after the fifth, press the right half center and drag 120 pixels right, then lift.
play_sequence.wait: After each seam, check that its marker changes; after the last, watch the split and crystals appear while pulling. There is no fixed timer.
play_sequence.expected: Seam taps are individually recorded; only then can the right half move. The pull opens the geode and completes at 120 pixels.

play_sequence.beat: Check state recovery and replay appeal
play_sequence.input: Interrupt a partial river stroke by lifting, then re-enter the same phase and confirm the wet section remains; after all four work verbs and the stage response, pause and let the child decide whether to repeat a favorite.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for save/re-entry and any completion flourish to settle; do not impose a session-duration target from the probe.
play_sequence.expected: Released partial material restores without a held pointer, malformed checkpoint data gives no phantom progress, and the final replay choice is left to the child.

source_constants.value: River path is a 9 by 5 grid with 88 by 76 pixel cells and a 46 pixel brush radius; any wet connected route from spring to finish completes, not only the suggested bent path.

Fossil brushing uses an 8 by 5 grid and advances at 26 cleared cells; three pieces snap when released within 92 pixels of their target. Pan counts nine direction reversals after a same-direction run of at least 46 pixels.
Geode requires five seam taps, each with a 56 pixel hit radius and press-to-release movement no greater than 34 pixels, then a 120 pixel rightward pull.
The scripted probe simulates 30 seconds of zero-input per mode, then prescribed gestures; its _process simulation uses 0.25 second increments. These are test inputs, not measured child pacing.

timing.assumptions: No child activity duration is estimated. The helper's 57.187 second wall time is probe execution only. The demo animation repeats on a 2.4 second code cycle (scripts/opera_geology_surface.gd:943-976), but speech duration, travel, rendered response latency and child pace were not measured.

tactile.target_size: The full-canvas surface is 1280x720 in the probe and its work area is Rect2(330,130,860,490) (scripts/opera_geology_surface.gd:11,2570-2573). Pan interaction accepts a grown work rect; fossil pieces use 130x234 rectangles grown 24 pixels; geode seam hit radius is 56 pixels (scripts/opera_geology_surface.gd:29-35,280-288,466-475,515-520). The geode's visible seam dot is radius 22 and halo radius 32 (lines 824-834), smaller than its code hit radius; actual projected size and child accuracy need Mobile/device review. The river path points are on an 88x76 cell grid with a 46 pixel brush radius (lines 11-16).
tactile.press_response: Accepted touches call _press immediately; changed river/fossil/pan/geode material updates fill, a positive feedback anchor, a 0.24 second feedback timer, and redraw (scripts/opera_geology_surface.gd:264-289,399-414,445-464,477-500,502-512,528-537). Probe assertions establish state transitions, not visible response within two rendered frames.
tactile.drag_hold_release: River and fossil brush interpolate the path between drag events; fossil assembly carries a selected piece and snaps on release within 92 pixels. Pan registers direction changes after a 46 pixel run. Geode tap-seam commits on release if the candidate stayed within 34 pixels; once all five are done, dragging the right half opens it (scripts/opera_geology_surface.gd:292-344,399-464,477-512).
tactile.ownership: Screen touch start claims touch_owner; drag and release are accepted only for that index, and a second press is ignored while an owner exists (scripts/opera_geology_surface.gd:347-360). Probe verifies a second finger cannot advance or steal a river stroke, then cancellation resets owner and held state (scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:2587-2599).
tactile.cancellation: Focus loss or app pause calls cancel_input; it clears held ownership, fossil drag, pan run and geode candidate/pull state without progressing the task (scripts/opera_geology_surface.gd:225-237,379-383). Probe covers explicit cancellation for a held river stroke but not a real pause/focus-loss event (scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:2594-2599).

play_appeal.hypothesis: The four verbs offer useful tactile variety: connect water, reveal and assemble a fossil, swish a pan, and pry open a crystal. The river accepting any connected spring-to-finish path gives room for a child's own route; the changing material and crystal reveal could invite another phase. The repeated generic voice event on RIVER/PAN/GEODE may make it less clear what each new touch should do. These are source-based hypotheses, not observed child reactions.
play_appeal.agency_test: During a normal routed session, leave a small disconnected wet patch and observe whether the child joins it to the spring-to-finish stream without losing progress; then offer the geode's visible seam markers and observe whether they infer tap-then-pull from voice/demo alone. After completion, provide no adult suggestion and record whether they choose to revisit a mode or leave.

play_sequence.appeal_test: This establishes tested mechanics only; it does not show the child can reach this route from a fresh save.

play_sequence.appeal_test: Travel direction follows each stroke, and the same movement does not accidentally invoke a world tap.

tactile.target_size: The tested movement region is a broad lower-left movement_zone, sampled 30 px inside its bounds; this probe does not measure the phone-projected size or other child-facing targets.
tactile.press_response: A movement-zone press alone leaves stick_vec at zero in the tested agreement loop. On release without a drag, hybrid mode sends the original press point to world_touched, so this region remains a world tap surface.

tactile.ownership: The router tracks owners by finger index; the stress probe's randomized churn checks for leaked owners/stick/action state, but this particular focused probe does not establish real multi-touch behavior on hardware.
tactile.cancellation: Focused route checks cover manual steering and pause cancellation of a pending Lagoon goal/focus. Focus loss and real device cancellation were not exercised here.

play_appeal.hypothesis: The movement region has a forgiving grammar: press-and-release can tap the world, while a deliberate drag steers in the direction the finger travels. This could make quick exploration feel immediate and recoverable, especially if a child sees Roshan respond promptly.
play_appeal.agency_variety_world_response_replay: The code and probe support distinct tap, hold, and drag travel cases and verify the route responds; they do not establish that the child understands the gesture difference, enjoys it, or wants to replay it.

Observe whether they intentionally retarget left then right, notice the travel direction matches the finger, and release without adult prompting; repeat once after leaving and returning. Record native video/input trace and child comprehension separately.

timing.assumptions: No child play duration or route pacing is inferred. The helper's 12.036-second wall time is probe execution time only.

tactile.target_size: The actor touch radius is 114 design-canvas pixels (228-pixel diameter footprint metadata) in scripts/arena/sky_lagoon_promenade.gd:23, 633. The probe checks a 110-pixel offset around the center (scripts/probe_sky_lagoon_animals.gd:87-98); physical size at target-device scale is unmeasured.
tactile.press_response: Code routes a promenade world tap to handle_touch (scripts/main.gd:4608-4612); a tap within the animal radius starts its startle sequence and is consumed (scripts/arena/sky_lagoon_promenade.gd:344-350). The probe calls _startle_animal directly, so routed press latency/feel was not tested.

tactile.ownership: This classic scripted probe does not make touch-ownership claims. The one-touch route policy is defined by DL-UI-04, but this run does not deliver concurrent or routed touches.
tactile.cancellation: The probe does not pause, lose focus, or cancel a routed animal tap. Existing route cancellation code clears walk goals and focus in scripts/arena/sky_lagoon_promenade.gd:371-389; its animal-specific interaction lifecycle was not exercised through UI.

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: a reachable small animal responding to a deliberate tap can make the long Lagoon walk feel inhabited and responsive. The configured radius is forgiving, and the response appears distinct from movement taps because animal hits take priority in handle_touch; actual agency was not observed.
play_appeal.variety: Five authored species rotate by three camera pages: otter/frog at page 0, hare/squirrel at page 1, raccoon at page 2. A single pooled sprite changes species by page and cycle (scripts/arena/sky_lagoon_promenade.gd:89-127, 623-643, 1274-1279). L36 asserted the roster but directly selected each animal.
play_appeal.world_response: The code specifies a short alert, squash, hop and retreat along the safe habitat path; the probe asserted the first three atlas frames and that all tested escape routes finish hidden at the safe endpoint. This is a plausible readable response, pending visual and child observation.
play_appeal.replay: Hypothesis: seeing a different local species after walking to another page may reward revisiting the promenade. The current page roster and 5.5-second respawn are code facts; repeated natural visits were not observed.
play_sequence: Beat 1: From a clean save, use only the normal on-screen Continue/start controls and ordinary progression to reach Sky Lagoon; do not call probe helpers. Record arrival cue and the first visible route landmark.

Beat 2: Wait 0.70 seconds after entering the animal's page (page spawn constant at scripts/arena/sky_lagoon_promenade.gd:24); observe whether an animal appears on the ground and whether Roshan can still be distinguished.

Beat 3: Tap once at the center of the animal; wait 0.24 seconds, then another 0.18 seconds, then another 0.24 seconds. Observe the alert, squash and hop response against the contact shadow (constants :26-28; frame timing asserted in scripts/probe_sky_lagoon_animals.gd:308-317).

Beat 4: Keep hands off until the animal follows its safe return path and disappears; observe whether the retreat reads as an intentional reaction rather than a lost or stuck character (scripts/arena/sky_lagoon_promenade.gd:1395-1416).
Beat 5: Wait 5.5 seconds after it hides and observe whether the page's next species appears (constant :25; roster cycle :1314-1338).
Beat 6: Tap empty ground once and let Roshan walk toward the next page; observe that empty-space movement still works and the animal tap did not steal movement control (touch routing :347-355).

Beat 7: Repeat one deliberate animal tap on each of two different pages, then return to the first page. Concrete appeal test: ask the child, without coaching, to show which animal they want to greet again and allow a self-chosen repeat; record whether they point/tap, wait through the response, and choose to revisit, without assigning a numeric fun score.

route_status.proven_scope: The exact Godot 4.7.2.stable probe passed its habitat roster, ground/path negative cases, cell-foot contacts, complete patrols, startles, tap-radius metadata, arrival-plane gating, roster return, and day/night tint assertions (receipt PASS; probe log ends SKY_LAGOON_ANIMALS|ALL OK).
route_status.route_gaps: The probe clears the start menu/story and enters the Lagoon by direct helper calls, writes lagoon_plane_departed, repositions the camera with set_master_route_x, binds species directly, and triggers startle directly. It does not reach the Lagoon through the ordinary progression or deliver an actual routed touch. Therefore approach discoverability, visible-device animal placement, real input response, and a child's return experience are not proven.

This probe does not show that any stale callback is harmless after resumption or activity exit.

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: a prominent Back to Play action plus optional picture-first collections may let a young player take a break and choose to return without treating pause as failure. L37 only checks control presence and scripted state toggles, so this is not observed child preference.

play_appeal.world_response: Pause source clears owned touch state and the tree pause state stops ordinary gameplay; no rendered character/world freeze, stale action, sound, or resume response was observed in this headless run.
play_appeal.replay: Not assessed. Probe reopens no activity and does not test a voluntary return after leaving the sheet.

route_status.proven_scope: The unchanged probe_ui_system passed once on exact Godot 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf with an isolated save profile at the frozen baseline. Its pause section sets main.game and phase, calls main.toggle_pause() directly, checks pause state/layer and large menu targets, then calls main.toggle_pause() again and checks unpause/layer restoration. Source review also traced live global-navigation and cancellation handlers.
route_status.route_gaps: The probe constructs this as a fixture: it sets Sky Lagoon root state directly and never presses the visible GlobalNavigationButton, the Resume button, or a gameplay target during the pause section. It does not send a held touch, release after resume, fire a delayed callback, or exercise activity teardown. The matrix's 'live' hint is not route evidence. No Mobile-rendered view, physical target phone, child session, or owner acceptance was observed.

play_sequence.expected: The activity opens and the instruction is spoken. Chapter Two/Opera fresh-save route access remains a separate open gap (MA-PLAY-005).

play_sequence.expected: The probe's direct Brawl entry requests huluu_greet and confirms its exact clip; its scripted state transition requests huluu_talk and preserves the message and segment state (probe_voice.gd:104-134, log:16-27).

play_sequence.input: In the scripted dialogue sequence with 9.0-second holds, tap once to advance First to Second, tap once to advance Second to Third, then tap once to exhaust the queue.
play_sequence.wait: No fixed wait is needed before each tap; the probe checks immediate skip consumption. If testing auto-advance instead, each configured hold is 9.0 seconds in this fixture, not a measured child-paced duration.
play_sequence.expected: Each tap stops the prior exact clip, starts only the next, and the final tap clears dialogue state (probe.log:32-42).

play_sequence.beat: Check no stale voice survives leaving
play_sequence.input: Leave the activity or invoke its normal teardown after a line starts; listen through the transition without touching again.
play_sequence.wait: Wait until the transition completes; L38 provides no measured route/transition duration.

play_sequence.beat: Run the appeal check without prompting
play_sequence.input: After the child hears and acts on one exact objective, remain quiet and let them choose to repeat, continue, or leave.
play_sequence.wait: Allow the child to decide at their own pace; no session duration is inferred.
play_sequence.expected: Record independent action, attention to the matching world response, and any voluntary request to replay. This is a proposed child study, not evidence collected in L38.

source_constants.value: Ordinary HUD messages set a 5.0-second message timer; Opera exact-voice messages clear the text and timer, while a missing exact clip leaves the adult reading caption visible for 5.0 seconds.

Dialogue advances after the requested hold, with a minimum 0.8-second hold and default 3.2 seconds; any touch can skip the current line. The probe supplies 9.0-second holds and explicitly skips three lines.
The helper finished in 8.618 seconds of wall time. This is probe execution only and is not gameplay or voice duration.

timing.assumptions: No child session length or recorded clip duration was inferred. Source timers are game-time settings; actual voice start latency, audibility, and duration were not measured on a device.

tactile.target_size: No rendered touch targets or phone projection were measured. The probe sets touch_ui.action_just directly for a simulated Brawl route event and calls skip_dialogue directly; it does not send routed screen-touch events (scripts/probe_voice.gd:99-106,140-165).
tactile.press_response: The probe verifies one dialogue skip advances the queue and stops the prior player before starting the next. It does not time a visible response to a routed touch or verify the displayed caption/character pointer during play (probe.log:32-42).
tactile.drag_hold_release: Not part of the voice focus and not exercised by this probe.
tactile.ownership: No touch index or second-finger ownership was tested. Dialogue skip accepts a touch through the caller, but L38 invokes skip_dialogue directly (scripts/audio_director.gd:443-447; scripts/probe_voice.gd:147,153,159).

play_appeal.hypothesis: An exact spoken instruction paired with an actionable event may let a non-reader act without stopping to decode a caption; serial playback and touch-skippable dialogue can also keep guidance from feeling like a barrier. These are design hypotheses. L38 did not hear the clips or observe a child, so it cannot establish warmth, comprehension, confidence, or enjoyment.
play_appeal.agency_test: On the target phone, give a child the voice-only exact objective at ordinary volume with captions hidden, then wait without pointing or repeating it. Record whether they begin the intended action, whether the matching character/object response makes the result clear, and whether after the activity they independently ask to hear/play another cue or choose to leave. Repeat once with audio disabled and only the adult reading caption to distinguish the support path; do not interpret either as child evidence until actually observed.

The matrix labels the source live, but this invocation itself did not traverse a visible route.

sessions.focus: Fetch mechanic vs missing child route

play_sequence.scope: The first six beats reconstruct the exact probe stimulus and phase waits, not a child playthrough. The last two state the concrete routed appeal test still needed.

beats.wait: Probe waits two process_frame calls after instantiating main, calls _skip_intro, waits one process_frame, directly selects the fetch friend record, then calls _start_game and waits one process_frame (probe_fetch.gd:4-22).
beats.input: No routed user input; direct internal launch.
beats.expected: Initial aim phase; the retained log records f=1 phase=aim round=0 miss=0.

beats.wait: While phase is aim, sample every frame; use the current aim_dir and frame counter. No fixed human wait is defined by the source.
beats.input: Set touch_ui.action_down true exactly when aim_dir is nonzero, aim_dir.x < 0.1, and fcount % 12 < 6; otherwise false (probe_fetch.gd:32-36). This is synthetic held state, not a tap event.
beats.expected: First throw; log changes to fly at f=65.

beats.wait: Release the synthetic action immediately after aim; wait for the ball landing and fetch/pickup/return phases, with no input during those phases (probe_fetch.gd:35-37).
beats.input: None until phase returns to aim.
beats.expected: Log records fetch at f=102, pickup at f=108, return at f=128, then aim round=1 at f=140.

beats.wait: Again sample aim_dir once per frame; safe cue dwell is continuous and miss-dependent (fetch.gd:219-245).
beats.input: Repeat the same exact action_down condition as beat 2; release outside aim.
beats.expected: Second throw; log changes to fly at f=234.

beats.wait: Wait without action through landing, pickup and return (probe_fetch.gd:35-37).
beats.expected: Log records fetch at f=271, pickup at f=282, return at f=302, then win at f=312.

beats.wait: For a future child test, wait for the visible green/safe arrow and its transition chime; no fixed seconds are promised.
beats.input: One brief finger press on the visible THROW control; lift before the ball lands.
beats.expected: Determine whether the child connects the cue to the throw without reading the caption or adult prompting; not tested here.

beats.wait: If the child throws into the lake, wait through the splash message and for the next aim cue.
beats.input: No corrective input during the splash; then one new press when the safe cue appears.
beats.expected: Determine whether the child stays willing to retry and understands the broadened safe area; no miss path occurred in this probe.

beats.wait: After retrieving the second ball, allow the friend response and return/exit choice to appear.
beats.input: No adult prompt; observe whether the child asks to play again or chooses a clear exit.
beats.expected: Concrete appeal test: with the live route exposed, have a non-reader play the full two-round loop on the target phone, including one natural miss if it occurs; note cue comprehension, voluntary retry/replay, confusion, and any adult help. No such child test was run.

code_constants.value: Aim sweep angular rate = 0.9 * pow(0.72, miss_count) radians per game second; safe-side sweep width is 1.25 initially, 0.85 at two misses, and 0.55 at three or more misses.
code_constants.scope: Code values only. The green interval varies with miss count and is not a fixed child wait.

code_constants.value: pickup_t starts at 0.8 seconds; ball attaches at pickup_t <= 0.35 seconds; Chuck movement is capped at 40 world units per game second.
code_constants.scope: Source constants, not observed real-time timing; the probe runs Engine.time_scale = 6.

timing.assumptions: No child-session duration or seconds-per-probe-frame estimate is reported. The helper's 10.469-second wall time is only probe execution time.

tactile.press_response: In code, the action press starts the ball's fly phase and hides the arrow in the same tick (scripts/games/fetch.gd:246-256). The headless run does not establish rendered-frame response or device latency.
tactile.drag_hold_release: No drag or release gesture is authored for aiming; the player waits for the moving safe cue and presses THROW. The handler reads the action as a held level while aim is active (scripts/games/fetch.gd:246-249); probe_fetch forces action_down false outside aim (probe_fetch.gd:32-36), so held-through-flight behavior is untested.

tactile.cancellation: Pause, focus-loss, exit cancellation and stale-action behavior are not asserted by probe_fetch.

play_appeal.world_response: Hypothesis: the shrinking safe-side challenge and a visible, animated Chuck could make the throw feel connected to a friend. Current source creates an empty Node3D Chuck root with a null AnimationPlayer, so the visible retrieval response is not established.
play_appeal.replay: Not assessed; this probe ends when the second round wins and does not test an ordinary child-facing replay or return route.

route_status.proven_scope: The unchanged probe_fetch run passed on Godot 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf. Its retained log records aim → fly → fetch → pickup → return twice and END game= won=true at frame 312 with zero misses.

The only _start_game call sites reviewed are the Day One dust-boss handoff and the Chapter Two rainbow-slide helper (main.gd:6753, 7080), neither of which launches Fetch. No visible Wacky/Chuck entry, routed touch, natural exit/re-entry, or ordinary save lifecycle was exercised.
route_status.normal_route_status: DORMANT; source mechanics exist behind the internal launcher, but child reachability is not shown by the minigame catalog row or this probe.

sessions.focus: Dolls mechanic vs missing child route

Focus loss, pause during a held touch, and OS-canceled touch were not exercised.

sessions.focus: Melody rhythm recovery and input variety

play_sequence.input: Once a real child-facing Daddy route exists, enter it and let the child watch the opening stage, Roshan, Daddy, pointer and first moving note without instruction.
play_sequence.wait: Allow the authored 0.25-second reveal tween to clear, then observe until the next green crossing; the note path repeats every 4.2 seconds.
play_sequence.basis: The production start uses a 0.25-second fade and Melody supplies the exact target+verb voice, pointer and green timing window (scripts/main.gd:3032-3048; scripts/games/melody.gd:47-48,657-685,688-713). This route is dormant and was not proven in the probe.

play_sequence.input: Invite one deliberate one-finger tap on the active note while it is inside the green zone; lift at the same location while it remains green.
play_sequence.wait: Wait only for the next rendered frame to confirm progress; if the child misses the window, allow the note to complete its 4.2-second cycle before the next attempt.
play_sequence.basis: The probe asserts one fresh in-green touch release scores exactly once; a missed full pass does not advance, reset, or fail (scripts/games/melody.gd:688-713,1196-1225; scripts/probe_melody.gd:1549-1570; runtime/L42/attempt_1/probe.log:119-123).

play_sequence.input: Let the child follow the new note and repeat the same press-and-release action for notes two through four, without telling them the timing.
play_sequence.wait: Each correct note starts a fresh 4.2-second cycle; observe each crossing and check for one new pip after each successful release.
play_sequence.basis: Success advances the active note and resets cycle time; the note/pip sequence preserves the seven-color order (scripts/games/melody.gd:1156-1169,1245-1264; runtime/L42/attempt_1/probe.log:240-245).

play_sequence.input: If a tap lands outside the active note or starts too early, let the child see the note pass and decide whether to try again; do not correct their hand.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for the next 4.2-second note pass; the probe also holds one early touch across the green interval and confirms it does not score.
play_sequence.basis: Wrong-point/early input and early-held input preserve progress and leave the activity live; no penalty is applied (scripts/games/melody.gd:722-733,1191-1193,1217-1225; scripts/probe_melody.gd:1539-1582; runtime/L42/attempt_1/probe.log:119-124).

play_sequence.input: Continue with one tap-and-lift for notes five and six; record whether the child notices changing colors, rising chime pitch and filled pips.
play_sequence.wait: Wait one 4.2-second cycle per missed note; after a correct release, the next note starts its own cycle immediately.
play_sequence.basis: The controller keeps the same timing verb but changes the active note color and raises chime pitch as progress increases (scripts/games/melody.gd:23-31,1245-1264; runtime/L42/attempt_1/probe.log:244-247).

play_sequence.input: On the seventh note, let the child make the final in-green press/release and observe whether they recognize Roshan/Daddy's completion response.
play_sequence.wait: Allow one next rendered frame for the synchronous completion transition; the probe asserts completion at note seven without a timer or fail branch.
play_sequence.basis: The last score calls the normal game-end path and completion cheer; the probe confirms no fail/timer branch (scripts/games/melody.gd:1254-1260; scripts/probe_melody.gd:2254-2264; runtime/L42/attempt_1/probe.log:246-249).

play_sequence.input: After the reward, leave the child free to choose replay or the neutral Back exit; note the choice and whether they can return without adult/debug navigation.
play_sequence.wait: Do not impose a timer on the child's decision. The probe's replay starts a new zero-of-seven stage; it is not evidence that the child can discover that route.
play_sequence.basis: Probe checks clean pause-menu leave and clean replay with medal upgrade but no duplicate trophy (scripts/probe_melody.gd:227-270,287-320,314-421; runtime/L42/attempt_1/probe.log:178-184,237-272).

A fresh press/release in green is the demonstrated child-facing verb. Actual finger drift tolerance is unknown.
tactile.ownership: The controller accepts one held source at a time and requires the matching source and kind to finish it; the probe checks that unrelated key/pad/touch releases cannot finish another held source (scripts/games/melody.gd:1184-1193,1196-1225; scripts/probe_melody.gd:1584-1612,2237-2246; runtime/L42/attempt_1/probe.log:128-151). Synthetic source IDs do not prove Android multitouch behavior.

All are scripted events; physical OS cancellation/focus behavior remains open.

The authored objective is 'Tap each rainbow note in the green!' and the probe verifies the voice resource/path, but neither sound nor child interpretation was observed (scripts/games/melody.gd:47-48,683-685; scripts/probe_melody.gd:1469-1494; runtime/L42/attempt_1/probe.log:49-50).

tactile.target_size: Snow face controls are checked against StorybookUI.MIN_TOUCH; the carrot button is 150×110 and coal buttons use that minimum (scripts/games/picture_games.gd:407-416; scripts/probe_mg2d.gd:168-185; runtime/L43/attempt_1/probe.log:36). Garden's 140×140 seed hit buttons, trampoline's 400×140 target, and Christmas ornaments at 110×110 meet the 110×110 base-canvas guideline in source (scripts/games/picture_games.gd:585-601,673-679,770-777; design/06_COMPREHENSIVE_DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md:714-716). This is source geometry only; no phone-projected or finger-occlusion measurement was made.
tactile.press_response: Garden, face-piece, trampoline and ornament interactions use Button signals or direct screen-touch handlers; the probe emits pressed signals and synthetic input. It checks visible growth and feedback counters, not rendered response within two frames or audible chimes on a device (scripts/games/picture_games.gd:407-416,615-656,683-714,781-797; scripts/probe_mg2d.gd:196-239; DL-AGE-07).
tactile.drag_hold_release: Garden, trampoline and Christmas are tap actions. Snowman offers circular drawing around the snowball, virtual-stick circles, and later a held-direction assist; a single circle-direction jump is clamped to 0.32 radians per frame to ignore teleport-like motion (scripts/main.gd:5634-5666,5677-5687). The probe uses the stick vector for rolling/chase, not a physical finger trace (scripts/probe_mg2d.gd:163-195).
tactile.ownership: Open/close state and feedback tweens are tied to the current picture-game stage, and a win-close callback checks both generation and root identity before closing (scripts/games/picture_games.gd:20-33,274-321). The probe checks cleanup and fresh-stage state across four opens (scripts/probe_mg2d.gd:129-160,289-315,324-325; runtime/L43/attempt_1/probe.log:53). This is scripted lifecycle evidence only.
tactile.cancellation: Back/pause paths eventually call _mg2d_close; close kills the win and feedback tweens and frees the stage (scripts/games/picture_games.gd:293-321). The focused probe exercises close/re-entry cleanup but does not establish natural Android focus loss, real multitouch cancellation or child recovery.

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: the family varies the child's verb—circle, tap a visible plant, bounce, chase, choose face pieces, or decorate—so agency may come from changing hand action rather than merely changing art. The scripted probe supports distinct state transitions but gives no child appeal evidence.
play_appeal.variety: Four stages are exercised in the probe: snowman, garden, trampoline and xmas. Slide is a fifth listed picture route but delegates to the full Lagoon slide activity and is not included in this probe loop (scripts/probe_mg2d.gd:133-136; scripts/games/picture_games.gd:14-19,719-760).
play_appeal.world_response: Source has immediate object changes: snowballs grow/stack, flowers change from seed to sprout to distinct flowers, Roshan bounces toward the star, and ornaments appear at fixed tree spots (scripts/games/picture_games.gd:381-404,615-656,696-714,781-797).
play_appeal.replay: Hypothesis: visible completed garden flowers and varied manual actions could invite replay, but source closes completed sessions and no child-initiated replay choice is tested (scripts/games/picture_games.gd:257-290; scripts/probe_mg2d.gd:289-325).

route_status.proven_scope: One unchanged invocation of probe_mg2d passed on Godot 4.7.2-stable with an isolated save profile. It directly calls _mg2d_open for snowman and then garden, trampoline and xmas, drives state/touch-like input from code, and checks completion, feedback and teardown (scripts/probe_mg2d.gd:71-99,133-160,196-249,289-329; runtime/L43/attempt_1/receipt.json; runtime/L43/attempt_1/probe.log:27-53).
route_status.route_gaps: The matrix labels this family dormant. main.gd retains a legacy court:picture callback into _touch_open_picture and PIC_GAME artwork mappings, but this probe bypasses that caller and starts each game directly; the source routes p_slide to _l2_start_slide, and the tested loop omits slide (audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/matrix.json L43; scripts/main.gd:4836-4851,5836-5839; scripts/games/picture_games.gd:14-19; scripts/probe_mg2d.gd:133-136). These references establish code wiring, not a current ordinary child-discovery route. No child-visible entry/exit/re-entry path is proven. Headless scripted success is not Mobile rendering, physical touch, child comprehension/fun or owner acceptance; the helper's wall time is not game duration.

play_appeal.hypothesis: I expect the visible slide, swing, and seesaw to invite a self-chosen short play loop: approach, tap twice, watch Roshan visibly use the selected toy, then move on or repeat. The four authored poses and equipment motion could make each choice feel distinct, while a long automatic action could reduce control for a preschooler.
play_appeal.concrete_appeal_test: On the target tablet, give a child a short uncoached visit with all three toys visible; record whether the child independently approaches and activates more than one, watches or interrupts the full action, returns to a toy, and can leave for the castle without adult prompting. Ask for no numeric fun rating; capture the child's spontaneous words/actions and separate observer interpretation.

route_status.proven: The unchanged probe entered Sky Lagoon twice, waited 12 frames after first entry and 4 frames after each build, and verified a single CanvasLayer, no spatial descendants, twelve backdrop tiles, four playground/door target IDs, and synchronous removal of the previous layer before the replacement remained live (scripts/probe_l2_reenter.gd:48-93; receipt log).
route_status.gaps: Probe setup directly sets pearl_count, friend wins, trophies, and plane departure, then invokes entry methods. It does not prove a child-visible route into the playground, toy activation/settle, external activity return, or actual touch/device rendering. The focused probe only exercises re-entry lifecycle.

play_sequence.input: Direct main._close_wardrobe() call; no global Back gesture/key.

timing.gameplay_estimate: Assumption: the game target is 30 fps, so the 0.6-second controller grace is about 18 frames; the 0.68-second sparkle fade is about 20 frames and the 2.2-second locked-look toast hold is about 66 frames. These source-window estimates are not observed child timing. Probe frame waits are explicit test synchronization, not a measured play session; helper wall time is not gameplay duration.
timing.probe_windows: The wardrobe leg opens and waits 1 process frame before checking UI; synthetic look picks run sequentially, then cleanup waits 2 frames. Re-entry waits 1 frame. The global controller path has a 0.6-second overlay grace before A/B acts.

tactile.target_size: Each wardrobe look button is 480x110 logical stage pixels; the finish button is 330x132. Probe checks the finish target's minimum thumb size, but phone-projected size and actual touch geometry were not measured.
tactile.press_response: A synthetic pressed signal immediately changes selected skin, preview and player twirl in the probe; real press-to-feedback latency was not captured. A successful pick also plays a chime and starts a bounded preview burst.
tactile.drag_hold_release: Wardrobe is button-based; no drag gesture or hold-to-select is implemented or tested. The global controller B closes after overlay grace; pointer global Back behavior was not exercised by this probe.
tactile.ownership: Overlay creation pushes the wardrobe route and disables world controls; close removes the route and restores controls. Physical one-finger ownership and overlap behavior remain unmeasured.
tactile.cancellation: Close queues the CanvasLayer for freeing, immediately clears wardrobe_layer/state, kills a live feedback tween, and re-entry starts with an empty feedback layer. Focus loss and real touch cancellation were not exercised.

play_appeal.hypothesis: Pictured, mutually exclusive looks with a large preview can make choosing feel like a clear make-believe transformation. A visible try-on response and easy return may invite experimenting, but readable labels and three stacked choices may still matter to a non-reader.
play_appeal.agency_variety_world_response_replay: Code and probe confirm distinct selectable looks, live preview updates, a twirl, bounded sparkle feedback, and lifecycle cleanup. They do not show whether a child recognizes the pictured choice, discovers wardrobe entry/Back, or wants to revisit the looks.
play_appeal.concrete_appeal_test: On the Lenovo Tab M11 with a fresh-save build and no adult pointing, observe whether the child reaches the bedroom wardrobe, taps a pictured look, notices Roshan's changed appearance, tries a second look, and exits with the visible global Back control. Repeat after leaving and returning; capture the screen and touch trace and record prompts, missed taps, comprehension and spontaneous replay separately.

route_status.proven_scope: The existing probe instantiates the normal main scene and wardrobe, programmatically emits look-button pressed signals, checks preview/selection/skin/twirl and feedback, closes and reopens the overlay, and tests feedback-node/tween cleanup. The session helper reports PASS under Godot 4.7.2-stable; the retained log ends with UI_SYSTEM|RESULT|ALL OK.

The probe checks that there is no wardrobe-specific Back button and calls _close_wardrobe() directly. play_sequence.appeal_test: A real cold-start run should show the expected fresh arrival without a menu flash and preserve the archived prior save.

timing.gameplay_estimate: Assuming the authored waits map directly to elapsed runtime, a saved-game reset needs the 1.5-second arm delay plus a 0.8-second continuous hold, about 2.3 seconds after opening confirmation, aside from discovery and input time. This is a code/probe estimate, not an observed adult or child interaction time. The 0.08-second confirmation tap and 0.32-second partial hold are probe timings. Helper wall time is not gameplay duration.
timing.probe_windows: Probe scene setup waits 2 frames, skips intro if active, waits 4 frames, builds menu, then waits 3 frames. NEW GAME uses a 0.08-second press; disarmed START NEW uses 0.08 seconds; the probe then waits 1.7 seconds for arming. It holds 0.32 seconds, releases and waits 1.1 seconds to test cancellation; next it holds 1.1 seconds to cover the 0.8-second action, releases, and waits 2 frames. Recreated main waits 2 frames before menu build and 4 afterward.

tactile.target_size: The saved-game NEW GAME control is 340x118 logical base-canvas pixels (scripts/start_menu.gd:92-94); confirmation KEEP GAME and START NEW are each 300x118 (scripts/start_menu.gd:249-256). Probe does not measure phone-projected dimensions or real touch hit geometry.
tactile.press_response: Synthetic pointer press opens the confirmation sheet. START NEW is disabled at first; during a held synthetic press the fill grows, and early release resets it and pulses the hint. A full hold installs the fresh save. Physical press-to-feedback latency was not measured.
tactile.drag_hold_release: The destructive confirmation is hold-based: button_down starts a 0.8-second timer and button_up invalidates a premature hold. Probe confirms a 0.32-second partial hold is cancelled and a 1.1-second press passes the hold window. Dragging outside the button, pointer cancellation, and touch-up behavior on Android were not exercised.
tactile.ownership: This is a single-button press path; the probe delivers one synthetic mouse pointer at a time. Multi-touch ownership and focus-loss while holding were not tested.
tactile.cancellation: Keep Game hides confirmation and invalidates a hold; early button_up increments the serial and resets the bar. Focus loss, pause, scene interruption during the timer, and storage-write failure were not driven by this probe.

play_appeal.hypothesis: A clear Keep Game choice, visible growing bar, and fresh Day One arrival could make a grown-up-initiated reset feel deliberate while protecting the existing adventure. For a non-reader child, the text-heavy warning and the required 2.3-second arm-plus-hold gesture may be difficult to interpret; the child should not have to decide whether to replace saved progress.
play_appeal.agency_variety_world_response_replay: The old save remains archived and a completed reset begins with no finished Day One rooms. The probe proves these state changes but does not establish that the confirmation, hold cue, or adult archive recovery is understandable or inviting. Replay appeal is not applicable to the reset itself; the new adventure's later replay is outside this focus.
play_appeal.concrete_appeal_test: On the Lenovo Tab M11, test with a consenting adult operating the reset while the child observes, then test fresh-save startup separately with no adult pointing. Capture whether the adult sees the warning, locates Keep Game, maintains the hold without accidental cancellation, and can restore the archived generation using the documented grown-up process. For the child, observe whether Day One arrival is clear and whether play begins without reading or spoken adult instruction; record prompts and touch trace.

tactile.press_response: Code connects the Continue button's pressed signal to _continue_game; that handler checks has_saved_game, dismisses the menu, selects the saved mode and calls launch. The probe checks mode preparation and source wiring, not a button press or frame-level feedback.
tactile.drag_hold_release: Continue is an ordinary button press with no hold timer in the inspected handler. Drag-out/release and Android touch cancellation were not tested.
tactile.ownership: No real or synthetic pointer sequence was sent in this probe, so finger ownership and second-finger behavior are unmeasured.
tactile.cancellation: No in-flight Continue cancellation, scene interruption, focus loss, or storage error was driven.

play_appeal.hypothesis: A saved-game Continue button emphasized in gold and initially focused can make resuming feel like the obvious next step, while preserving a child-selected room. Returning to the same room could support agency if the saved location and room entrance are immediately recognizable; this remains an untested hypothesis because the probe does not load or display the route.
play_appeal.agency_variety_world_response_replay: The code maps a valid Day One room to its castle room and normalizes invalid saved rooms to a safe fallback. These are sensible orientation safeguards in source, but no world response, replay choice or understandable arrival was observed. Legacy saves without the Day One flag intentionally route outside Day One; that policy is asserted in the probe.
play_appeal.concrete_appeal_test: On a Lenovo Tab M11 using the exact approved build and a consented, non-identifying test save, film the ordinary boot-to-menu-to-Continue path for each representative bathroom/pool/stuffie/art saved location and one legacy save. After each single tap, check visible acknowledgment within two rendered frames, confirm the expected room/landmark and orientation without adult pointing, then let the player choose whether to act or leave. Repeat after a normal save/reopen; record adult help, misroutes, voluntary repeat choice and actual touch coordinates. Do not infer child appeal from machine PASS.

observations.title: Three or more simultaneous required prompts can exceed the two-entry queue
evidence: scripts/audio_director.gd:265-283 (when a required line is active, at most two distinct following required prompts are appended; further prompts have no enqueue path)

observations.reproduction: Source inspection confirms the required queue appends only while its size is below two, then returns without storing an additional distinct required event. L38 did not produce this burst, so this is a code-path risk rather than a runtime reproduction.
observations.child_impact: If a caller emits at least three distinct required instructions before the active speech ends, the last instruction can be lost; a non-reader could miss the action needed to continue. The ordinary occurrence rate is unknown.
observations.proposed_repair: Trace all same-frame required prompt callers before changing queue policy. If multi-prompt bursts are valid, ensure every still-relevant objective is delivered or superseded deliberately rather than silently discarded.
observations.acceptance_test: A focused test should start one active required line, enqueue three distinct required lines before it finishes, and verify intentional coalescing or delivery of all still-relevant instructions in correct order without stale prompts or overlap.
