observations.child_impact: The spatial aim and swimming-era setup carries device and tactile/readability risk under the project's true-2D and one-finger requirements; no target-device evidence is available for it.
observations.proposed_repair: Do not revive the legacy spatial implementation. Any future authorized Fetch work should rebuild the bounded timing verb on Canvas using the accepted medium and art rules.
observations.acceptance_test: The converted Canvas activity must pass focused input/progression/passive/teardown/save probes, aspect-ratio runtime captures, actual M11 touch/performance checks, and separate child/owner reviews.

observations.title: Mercy widens the safe throw while preserving the child's next action
evidence: scripts/games/fetch.gd:219-228 reduces sweep rate after each miss and makes the safe sweep width 0.55 after three misses.
scripts/games/fetch.gd:281-286 gives a kind shake-off retry line after three splashes and returns to aim; it does not throw automatically.
scripts/games/fetch.gd:246-252 requires the action press before entering fly.
observations.reproduction: Code path only; the L39 probe had zero misses and did not execute the splash or three-miss assist branches.
observations.child_impact: If the cue is legible, the forgiving widening window can preserve a route after a miss without removing the child's choice to press again. Child comprehension and appeal are untested.
observations.proposed_repair: Retain the no-punishment, non-automatic mercy design during any future authorized conversion; verify the messages and cue in context.
observations.acceptance_test: Through routed touch, intentionally make one and then three safe-side misses; confirm kind feedback, slower/wider cue, continued child-controlled throws, and no loss or automatic win.

observations.title: The cue has visual and audio components in code, but its child meaning is unverified
evidence: scripts/games/fetch.gd:190 presents the text instruction to avoid the lake and press on green; :231-245 colors and swells the arrow and plays a chime on transition to safe snow.
scripts/main.gd:8375-8385 labels the contextual action THROW during aim.
The L39 log contains phase changes only; it has no rendered capture, audio playback assertion or routed touch trace.
observations.reproduction: Inspect the arrow/cue path and the log. The probe's synthetic condition uses aim_dir.x < 0.1 directly, so it does not show that a player can distinguish the green safe window or hear the chime.
observations.child_impact: If green/red or the chime is hard to notice at phone scale, a non-reader may throw randomly or need an adult to interpret the caption.
observations.proposed_repair: No cue redesign is justified by code alone. Validate the current redundant cue on the actual device through the authorized live route before proposing a change.
observations.acceptance_test: With captions ignored, the child independently points to or presses on the safe cue, sees the ball land on snow, and can recover after a miss; separately verify two-frame response and audible cue on the target phone.

observations.title: The catch loop is mechanically recoverable and requires intentional input
evidence: scripts/probe_dolls.gd:79-150 starts an internally prepared run, waits through two misses, and checks no catches or save progress from passive play; runtime/L40/attempt_1/probe.log reports those assertions and DOLLS|result: ALL OK.
scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:131-170 slows/retargets after misses and records safe landings without incrementing caught; :192-203 requires fresh input to catch.
audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/runtime/L40/attempt_1/receipt.json records PASS on Godot 4.7.2-stable, isolated profile, headless=true, rendered_mobile_acceptance=false.
observations.reproduction: The probe waits for two misses with no input and asserts caught==0, no progress changes, and that the game remains active. It then uses routed screen events in the positive loop to steer and catch three dolls.
observations.child_impact: A mistake does not lose a doll or award progress, and later attempts are easier while still requiring deliberate steering. Whether the child can discover the timely drag needed remains unobserved.
observations.proposed_repair: No mechanical repair is established by this pass. Preserve safe landings and intentional catches; assess the instruction and input cadence in the real route with a child.
observations.acceptance_test: On the target device, observe an uncoached child through two safe misses and three catches. Confirm they understand the cradle action, recover independently, and receive immediate visible/audible response without passive progress.

observations.title: The assigned probe tests routed touch events, but still constructs the run internally
evidence: scripts/probe_dolls.gd:52 forces friend['found']=true and :79 calls main._start_game(friend), so this is not proof of the fresh-save world route.

scripts/probe_dolls.gd:444-550 injects screen press, drag and release events through the viewport and checks the catcher position; runtime/L40/attempt_1/probe.log reports the three-doll verb assertion PASS.
scripts/main.gd:796-802 declares Faron's Dolls friend; :7873-7890 dispatches the game when called, but this session did not establish a normally reachable interaction path.
observations.reproduction: Read the focused setup and compare it with the dispatch code: the probe mutates found state and calls _start_game directly. Its injected input validates the surface after entry, not discovery/start from ordinary play.
observations.child_impact: A well-working optional activity is unavailable if a child cannot find and enter it through visible play. The assigned internal pass does not resolve whether this route gap exists in a shipping route.
observations.proposed_repair: No route implementation is claimed here. Trace the current production interaction graph and add an ordinary fresh-save route only if the missing route is confirmed in the authorized scope.
observations.acceptance_test: From a clean save, use only the normal game interface to encounter Faron, discover Dolls, enter, finish, leave and re-enter. Record every visible cue and input path, then collect separate device and child evidence.

observations.title: A missing spoken recording for the three-catch objective is explicitly surfaced
evidence: scripts/games/dolls.gd:246-255 fixes the goal at three, records objective_recording_gap='faron_catch_three', keeps a visual pointer, and displays the text greeting.
The source comment at scripts/games/dolls.gd:249-250 says the available Faron catch clip says five, so the semantically inaccurate clip is withheld.
runtime/L40/attempt_1/probe.log reports the picture-first pointer remains while the exact goal clip is missing.
observations.reproduction: Inspect build() metadata and greeting, then verify the probe's missing-goal-clip assertion. No voice recording was modified or approved by this review.
observations.child_impact: The spoken cue may not communicate the precise three-catch goal; a child may rely on picture progress or the supplemental text, whose comprehension was not tested.
observations.proposed_repair: Keep the inaccurate five-count line withheld. Treat a correct three-count recording as an outstanding voice-authority dependency; the code currently retains the visual pointer and generic greeting.
observations.acceptance_test: With the approved exact-goal recording available, verify the child hears and understands the three-catch cue without reading, while the pointer and three picture pips agree with actual progress. Until then, report the voice gap separately.

observations.title: Canvas fit and touch ownership have not been observed on the target display
evidence: scripts/games/dolls.gd:261-278 scales the 1024×608 surface to fit the viewport and positions it centrally.
scripts/opera_nursery_catch.gd:44-46 sets MOUSE_FILTER_STOP; :110-127 maps press/drag local x into cradle position.
The probe validates source transforms with synthetic viewport events (scripts/probe_dolls.gd:444-550); receipt states headless=true and rendered_mobile_acceptance=false.
observations.reproduction: The assigned probe produces no Mobile rendering and does not inject competing fingers, touch cancellation, pause, or focus-loss input. Receipt and source identify the limits.
observations.child_impact: A surface can be generous in source coordinates yet still feel offset or small after aspect-ratio scaling. A finger or overlay ownership issue could make a correct gesture appear ignored; neither was established here.
observations.proposed_repair: No code change is supported by this headless result. Review the visible surface and input ownership on the supported aspect ratios and target phone.
observations.acceptance_test: On Lenovo Tab M11, compare the painted cradle and responsive surface at supported aspects. Try one-finger press, drag, release, second finger, canceled touch, pause and exit; verify the correct finger controls the cradle and no stale action triggers.

observations.title: The internal replay proves medal improvement and exactly-once trophy behavior
evidence: scripts/probe_dolls.gd:260-290 waits for reward cleanup, re-enters a fresh surface, completes a no-miss replay, and checks gold upgrade without a second trophy.
runtime/L40/attempt_1/probe.log reports post-win re-entry, replay catches, medal upgrade and clean teardown all OK.
scripts/games/dolls.gd:317-347 ends at three catches and tears down its surface/control ownership.
observations.reproduction: The probe completes the first run after misses, waits 90 accelerated process frames, starts again, and completes a clean replay; persistent medal improves and trophy count remains unchanged.
observations.child_impact: The code supports an optional replay with a better medal and avoids duplicate trophy rewards. The child-facing choice to replay, save reload and route return were not observed.
observations.proposed_repair: No save or replay defect is shown by these assertions; retain additive persistence and exactly-once rewards.
observations.acceptance_test: From the ordinary route, win and leave, reload the save, replay, and confirm progress is retained, a better medal can be earned, and no duplicate trophy appears. Observe whether the child chooses this voluntarily.

observations.title: The standalone four-tree Seek activity has no proven ordinary entry route
evidence: The assigned matrix marks L41 route_state_hint dormant (audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/matrix.json:290-295).
The probe manually sets friend['found'] and invokes _start_game(friend), bypassing a visible route (scripts/probe_seek.gd:44-45,79-84).

Main retains the Seek dispatch, but non-probe _start_game call sites in main.gd are the dust-boss and rainbow-slide helpers; the separate Comfy mode wires visible buttons for its own hidden friends (scripts/main.gd:6753,7071-7081,7870-7895; scripts/comfy_games.gd:346-354,432-445).
observations.reproduction: Inspect all main.gd _start_game callers and the assigned probe setup. The probe starts Seek directly; no normal-world caller to this friend game appears in the inspected source. The matrix classifies the route as dormant.
observations.child_impact: A child cannot benefit from the otherwise-tested activity if they cannot discover and enter this standalone route. The distinct Chapter Two Comfy hide-and-seek is not evidence that this Evie/Lamb-a' Seek route works.
observations.proposed_repair: Do not change code based on this review alone. Intake the missing ordinary entry/re-entry route as a reachability candidate and assess it against MA-PLAY-001 before any scoped repair.
observations.acceptance_test: From fresh progress and an ordinary visible one-finger route, have a child reach the Evie/Lamb-a' four-tree activity, leave safely, return to the same world, re-enter, and resume without debug state changes or adult navigation.

observations.title: The available prompt confirms the verb but the protected Evie objective recording is still missing
evidence: Build displays the instruction to tap the wiggly tree while a source comment explicitly says the available Evie start recording lacks the exact tap verb (scripts/games/seek.gd:599-603).
The existing finding records the exact protected Evie recording gap and child comprehension acceptance requirement (audit/findings/ACTIVE_FINDINGS_2026-08-13.md:466-486).
The probe confirms the available generic Evie start clip is selected, not that it says the tree-tap instruction (scripts/probe_seek.gd:103-111; runtime/L41/attempt_1/probe.log).
observations.reproduction: Start the internal probe, listen to the Evie start cue in an actual device session, and compare it with the visible 'tap the wiggly tree' objective. This run only checks the selected resource path; it did not listen to audio.
observations.child_impact: The text tells a reader what to tap, and the wiggly tree/pointer support it, but a non-reader may still not know the requested action from the available voice cue alone. Device audibility and comprehension are untested.
observations.proposed_repair: Keep the existing protected source untouched. Resolve the authorized exact Evie objective recording under MA-ACCESS-003; preserve the coordinated visible pointer and existing speech path.
observations.acceptance_test: With authorized recording approval, verify the exact cue plays while the active tree and pointer are visible, is intelligible on the Lenovo Tab M11, and an observed child acts without reading or adult explanation.

observations.title: Wrong-tree taps are bounded feedback without loss or progress
evidence: The probe routes a wrong bush touch and asserts rustle state, one wrong-tap count, unchanged found count, and no reset of help time; its follow-up samples a visible wobble/scale/tint peak (scripts/probe_seek.gd:151-174).
Wrong feedback lasts 0.55 seconds and does not fill pips; wrong handler only increments its diagnostic count, plays feedback and returns (scripts/games/seek.gd:320-323,528-537,631-644).
The exact run ended SEEK|result: ALL OK; receipt records headless=true, isolated_profile=true, rendered_mobile_acceptance=false (runtime/L41/attempt_1/probe.log; runtime/L41/attempt_1/receipt.json).
observations.reproduction: The assigned probe selects the index after the active tree, routes a synthetic touch there, confirms no find/progress loss, and separately checks the peak visual feedback values.
observations.child_impact: A wrong choice has a short, visible response and does not punish or erase progress. Whether the child can distinguish helpful rustle from the target cue is not established without rendered/child review.
observations.proposed_repair: No mechanical defect is demonstrated; preserve the no-loss behavior and verify the two visual cues remain distinct on device.
observations.acceptance_test: On the supported phone, invite one wrong tap and one correct tap; confirm the wrong tree rustles briefly without a pip or lost progress, while the active tree's cue remains clear and usable.

observations.title: The four-find loop supports clean repeat and exactly-once reward semantics
evidence: The first routed run reaches four finds, persists bronze and one trophy, then tears down; the replay starts zeroed, reaches four more finds, upgrades to gold, and keeps trophy count unchanged (scripts/probe_seek.gd:249-320).
The probe log reports all first-run, post-win re-entry, replay-upgrade and teardown assertions OK (runtime/L41/attempt_1/probe.log).
The loop uses four targets and the next active tree excludes the previous one; successful reveal triggers cheer/clap states (scripts/games/seek.gd:6-7,301-313,653-675).
observations.reproduction: The assigned probe completes one slow first run, reads the saved medal/trophy state, re-enters the activity, completes a faster run and compares persistent state.
observations.child_impact: The mechanics can provide four successive reveals and a reason to improve a medal on replay without duplicate trophy farming. Child-paced completion, reward comprehension and voluntary replay are unknown.
observations.proposed_repair: No reward or teardown repair is indicated by this probe; preserve exactly-once trophy and better-medal replay behavior.
observations.acceptance_test: From a normal route, observe one complete round and voluntary replay; verify the child understands the filled pips/reward, the second round begins cleanly, a better medal persists and no second trophy is granted.

observations.title: Generous source-space targets and synthetic routing still need device confirmation
evidence: The probe checks four non-overlapping in-bounds target rectangles at least 110×110 canvas pixels (scripts/probe_seek.gd:400-413).
Its tap helper converts a target center through surface and viewport transforms and sends synthetic press/release events (scripts/probe_seek.gd:523-545).

The exact receipt explicitly states headless=true and rendered_mobile_acceptance=false; DL-QA-04/05 require device and child evidence (runtime/L41/attempt_1/receipt.json; design/06_COMPREHENSIVE_DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md:1253-1264).
observations.reproduction: Probe asserts the authored canvas rectangles and routes their centers; it does not render accepted Mobile captures or exercise actual fingers/aspect ratio on Lenovo Tab M11.
observations.child_impact: The code targets may be large in canvas coordinates yet their visible alignment, finger occlusion, latency, and child's ability to distinguish four options remain unknown.
observations.proposed_repair: No code change follows from synthetic geometry. Capture the exact route at supported device dimensions and observe the intended child before proposing hit-area/layout changes.
observations.acceptance_test: On Lenovo Tab M11, validate all four tree visuals and projected hit regions at the shipping aspect; observe uncoached one-finger taps, response latency, wrong-target recovery and play comfort.

observations.title: The Daddy Mermaid activity has no proven ordinary route after reef discovery retired
evidence: The assigned matrix marks L42 dormant (audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/matrix.json:298-303).
The probe says the reef discovery/PLAY route to Daddy retired on 2026-09-23 and calls _start_game directly (scripts/probe_melody.gd:158-159,2650-2656).

Main retains Daddy in FRIEND_DEFS and Melody dispatch, but its only non-probe _start_game callers found here launch the dust boss or rainbow slide (scripts/main.gd:797-804,6753,7071-7081,7870-7907). The run itself verifies only direct start (runtime/L42/attempt_1/probe.log:43-50).
observations.reproduction: Inspect the matrix row, probe setup and all production _start_game call sites. The assigned probe calls _start_game(daddy_friend) after choosing its FRIEND_DEFS record; no production caller supplies that friend record, and the probe comment identifies the old reef route as retired.
observations.child_impact: The seven-note timing activity can be entered only by direct setup in this evidence. A child may not discover it through ordinary visible play, so its timing, recovery and replay mechanics cannot yet benefit them through the normal route.
observations.proposed_repair: Treat as route/reachability candidate under MA-PLAY-001. No runtime change is authorized by this review; determine the intended visible entry/return route before evaluating child access.
observations.acceptance_test: From a fresh save on an exact candidate, let the child find Daddy through visible one-finger cues, enter Melody, complete or leave safely, return to the world and re-enter without reading, cheats, progress loss or adult/debug navigation.

observations.title: Seven notes repeat one timing verb while color and chime pitch supply the observed variation
evidence: The game defines seven ordered colors and one repeated note cycle; a successful score raises chime pitch and resets the next note's cycle (scripts/games/melody.gd:7-31,1245-1264).

The probe drives seven successful touches and a replay mixing Space, pad A and touch; its `ALL OK` establishes route assertions and state, not whether the child perceives enough variety (scripts/probe_melody.gd:2207-2264; runtime/L42/attempt_1/probe.log:240-266).
observations.reproduction: Read _score_current_note and run the assigned probe. Each note uses the same timing-zone action; the active color, pip progress and pitch change with count. The probe contains no child or appeal measurement.
observations.child_impact: The color/pitch progression may make repeated catches feel like building a rainbow, or the identical action may feel repetitive. No child response or voluntary replay was observed, so neither interpretation is confirmed.
observations.proposed_repair: Do not add mechanic variation based on this hypothesis alone. Observe an uncoached child through the seven-note run and let their attention, comprehension and replay choice determine whether the current progression sustains interest.
observations.acceptance_test: During a routed child session, record whether the child independently tracks the changed note, anticipates the next pass, notices filled pips/color/chime changes, and voluntarily continues through seven notes or requests another round.

observations.title: A missed or mistimed note recovers without punishment or passive completion
evidence: The probe asserts an early tap, a wrong-location tap during green, a complete passive missed pass, and an early-held touch crossing into green all leave progress unchanged and keep Melody live (scripts/probe_melody.gd:1539-1582; runtime/L42/attempt_1/probe.log:119-124).

The code arms only when press starts in green and, for touch, in the current hit rect; scoring requires same-source release while still green and still inside the touch hit rect (scripts/games/melody.gd:1172-1225).
The note recycles on a 4.2-second loop with no countdown/fail branch; probe asserts no passive completion (scripts/games/melody.gd:7,688-713,1245-1268; runtime/L42/attempt_1/probe.log:57-59,121-123).
observations.reproduction: The focused probe waits for a non-green frame, taps early, taps outside the note during a green frame, waits through a full missed window, then holds from early into green. Each negative check confirms no award, failure or lost live state.
observations.child_impact: A missed opportunity costs time until the note cycles back but does not erase progress or end the activity. This is a forgiving recovery path in code; the child-facing emotional response and whether the wait feels too long remain unobserved.
observations.proposed_repair: Preserve this no-fail recovery. Device/child observation should check that the next moving note remains obvious after a miss and that waiting a cycle is comfortable.
observations.acceptance_test: On the actual device, deliberately let a child miss one pass without prompting; confirm they recognize another chance, recover independently, retain prior pips and do not interpret the miss as losing.

observations.title: The source-space note target is generous, but phone fit and finger drift are not verified
evidence: The visible note is 84x84 while its active rectangle is 120x120; the probe checks layout and target geometry at 1280x720 and 1280x800 (scripts/games/melody.gd:10-11,953-957,1045-1092; scripts/probe_melody.gd:628-766).

Touch drag disarms after 48 pixels or when leaving the target/window; probe injects centered synthetic press/release events and checks state (scripts/games/melody.gd:722-733; scripts/probe_melody.gd:2207-2246).
Receipt states headless=true and rendered_mobile_acceptance=false; no physical touch or Lenovo Tab M11 result is present (runtime/L42/attempt_1/receipt.json).
observations.reproduction: The probe routes synthetic presses at the moving note center; source geometry gives a 120-pixel hit box and 48-pixel drag cancellation threshold. Neither actual thumb coverage nor natural finger drift is exercised.
observations.child_impact: A child may cover the small visible note while tapping or drift more than 48 pixels during the timed press; actual success rate and comfort on the intended phone are unknown.
observations.proposed_repair: No hit-area change follows from headless geometry alone. Check projected target size, finger occlusion and natural tap drift during the device session before proposing a source adjustment.
observations.acceptance_test: On the Lenovo Tab M11 at shipping aspect, measure the projected hit region and observe uncoached one-finger taps across all note positions, including a missed pass and natural finger drift; confirm response, comfort and ownership remain clear.

observations.title: Pause, overlay and focus restoration clear held input without scoring stale releases
evidence: The probe holds touch/key/pad sources across pause, sends wrong-source releases, resumes, and verifies only the original source can clear its latch and no stale release scores (scripts/probe_melody.gd:1584-1665; runtime/L42/attempt_1/probe.log:125-170).

It also simulates standalone/nested focus/application loss, restore guards, controller disconnect and fresh-source recovery; all listed checks are `MELODY|OK` (scripts/probe_melody.gd:1892-2206; runtime/L42/attempt_1/probe.log:174-239).
The production controller tracks exact source tokens and neutralizes input on context loss/cancel (scripts/games/melody.gd:750-821; scripts/main.gd:3361-3396,3707-3733).
observations.reproduction: The single run uses synthetic touch, key and pad events with real pause/resume controls and explicit focus/application notification calls, then asserts neutral cancellation and correct-source recovery.
observations.child_impact: The tested controller path avoids accidental scoring from stale or unrelated releases and permits a fresh gesture after recovery. Real Android lifecycle delivery and physical multitouch remain unverified.
observations.proposed_repair: No defect is demonstrated in the tested controller path. Keep the device matrix independent because scripted notifications do not prove Android's actual event ordering.
observations.acceptance_test: On device, hold a note press while pausing/backgrounding, resume with a second finger or unrelated control, and release the original owner; verify zero accidental score and that a fresh deliberate tap resumes play normally.

observations.title: Snowball circle action changes the object and has a bounded assist
evidence: Each ball initializes with 3, 2.5, then 2 required turns, and visibly grows with accumulated angular change (scripts/games/picture_games.gd:351-375; scripts/main.gd:5656-5667).

After 8 seconds without progress, assistance requires ongoing stick intent and adds progress; zero input is explicitly neutral (scripts/main.gd:5668-5687). The probe passed its zero-input/held-stick assist assertions (scripts/probe_mg2d.gd:77-90; runtime/L43/attempt_1/probe.log:27-28).
observations.reproduction: Source review plus the one unchanged probe invocation. The probe writes the stick vector directly and accelerates Engine.time_scale; it does not draw a physical circle or prove visible route entry.
observations.child_impact: The circle is a distinct motor action; the held-direction assist could help a child who attempted but cannot sustain the circle. Physical discoverability and comfort are unknown.
observations.proposed_repair: No code repair is evidenced. Include actual circular finger input and an attempted-but-stalled assist path in routed device and child review.
observations.acceptance_test: On the target phone, enter by the natural picture route; observe an uncoached circle gesture, object growth within two rendered frames, zero-input neutrality, and the 8-second assist after a real attempted stall.

observations.title: Four tested games have distinct, truthful object responses; the fifth is a separate Lagoon route
evidence: The probe directly opens snowman, garden, trampoline and xmas, then passes all four; its log records WON times under accelerated simulation and confirms garden flower retention (scripts/probe_mg2d.gd:133-160,196-239,289-325; runtime/L43/attempt_1/probe.log:29-53).

Source changes the affected objects: garden seed→sprout→flower and trampoline bounce toward the star; ornaments are placed at listed tree spots (scripts/games/picture_games.gd:615-656,696-714,781-797).
Slide is redirected to _l2_start_slide by _mg2d_open; the probe does not exercise that fifth family entry (scripts/games/picture_games.gd:14-19; scripts/probe_mg2d.gd:133-136).
observations.reproduction: Receipt shows PASS for probe_mg2d; the probe directly invokes open methods and advances frames at Engine.time_scale 6. Its WIN timings are not child timing evidence.
observations.child_impact: Distinct visible state changes may help make the actions understandable. The fifth route's completeness and ordinary discovery remain unverified.
observations.proposed_repair: No defect demonstrated in four tested mechanics. Cover the delegated Lagoon slide with its own routed lifecycle evidence and clarify whether the legacy picture wall remains a live child route.
observations.acceptance_test: From ordinary play, open all five destinations by visible route, perform each intended one-finger verb, verify correct object response and completion, then leave/re-enter without a debug call.

observations.title: Tap targets meet base-canvas geometry in source, while physical usability remains open
evidence: Garden has 140×140 seed hit buttons with 100px clear spacing; trampoline has a 400×140 art target; Christmas ornaments are 110×110 (scripts/games/picture_games.gd:585-601,673-679,770-777).

Snowman face buttons are checked against StorybookUI.MIN_TOUCH; probe logs the target-size assertion OK (scripts/games/picture_games.gd:407-416; scripts/probe_mg2d.gd:168-185; runtime/L43/attempt_1/probe.log:36).

The source sizes are compared with 110×110 guideline, but receipt is headless and says rendered_mobile_acceptance=false (design/06_COMPREHENSIVE_DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md:714-716; runtime/L43/attempt_1/receipt.json).
observations.reproduction: Static dimensions and one scripted face target check; no native-resolution rendered capture or physical phone interaction.
observations.child_impact: Nominal canvas hit regions look generous by the rule, but thumb occlusion, Android projection and neighboring target comfort have not been observed.
observations.proposed_repair: No hit-box change follows from headless dimensions. Measure on-device before changing layout.
observations.acceptance_test: On the intended phone, measure projected hit boxes and observe uncoached taps with natural thumb occlusion across each target, including near-misses and adjacent choices.

observations.title: Snowman, trampoline, garden and Christmas objectives rely heavily on on-screen text
evidence: The objectives and phase cues are label strings such as circle instructions, tap-the-carrot, trampoline directions, and Christmas ornaments (scripts/games/picture_games.gd:83-86,332-348,407-416,453-459,573-574,664-665,766-777).

Probe validates state progression, target sizes and feedback but does not check voice lines, a moving pointer, or comprehension (scripts/probe_mg2d.gd:66-71,133-185,196-240; runtime/L43/attempt_1/probe.log:27-53).
Non-reader objective guidance requires a spoken cue plus moving visual pointer or equally clear diegetic cue (design/06_COMPREHENSIVE_DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md:320-326).
observations.reproduction: Inspect objective strings and probe assertions. This is a coverage gap rather than confirmation that no voice or cue exists elsewhere; the route is dormant and no full child-facing screen was rendered.
observations.child_impact: If text is the only cue in any live phase, a non-reader may not know the intended action; whether scene art communicates it independently has not been assessed.
observations.proposed_repair: Review the complete live screens and voice routing before changing anything; add no substitute line without checking approved voice authority.
observations.acceptance_test: On device, observe whether a child starts and understands each verb without adult reading; separately verify an authorized voice cue and visible action cue for every objective.

observations.title: Win close is generation-bound and stage-owned, but routed interruption remains unverified
evidence: Win schedules a 1.6-second close callback bound to the opening generation and root; stale generation/root returns without closing a newer activity (scripts/games/picture_games.gd:274-290).

Close kills the close and feedback tweens, frees the stage and restores controls/music; the probe verifies four close/re-entry teardown cycles (scripts/games/picture_games.gd:293-321; scripts/probe_mg2d.gd:289-325; runtime/L43/attempt_1/probe.log:53).
observations.reproduction: Probe returns each opened test stage to a fresh stage and passes cleanup checks; no natural Back or Android interruption path is asserted in this focused source review.
observations.child_impact: A stale win callback should not close a later activity by the guarded code path. Whether a child can leave, pause and re-enter through visible controls remains unknown.
observations.proposed_repair: No lifecycle repair indicated by the scoped probe. Add routed Back/pause/re-entry coverage if this picture wall is confirmed live.
observations.acceptance_test: Win, leave during the payoff, open another activity, and confirm the old callback cannot close it; repeat with pause/background/foreground and verify progress safety.

observations.title: Re-entry replaces the prior promenade synchronously
evidence: scripts/probe_l2_reenter.gd:64-93; attempt_1/probe.log reports REENTER canvas_first: OK, canvas_rebuild_no_stack: OK, ALL OK
scripts/arena/sky_lagoon_promenade.gd:196-197,296-301
